sentences.zh: 【宋紀十六】　起柔兆執徐，盡著雍敦牂，凡三年。

translations.literal: [Song Records 16] From Rouzhao Zhixu through Zhuoyong Dunzang; three years in all.
translations.idiomatic: [Song Records 16] From Rouzhao Zhixu through Zhuoyong Dunzang—three years in all.

sentences.zh: 蒼梧王下元徽四年（

translations.literal: Deposed Emperor of Cangwu, lower scroll, Yuanhui year 4 (
translations.idiomatic: Deposed Emperor of Cangwu, lower scroll, Yuanhui year 4 (

sentences.zh: 丙辰，公元四七六年）

translations.literal: bingchen, 476 CE)
translations.idiomatic: bingchen, AD 476)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，己亥，帝耕籍田，大赦。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on jihai the emperor plowed the sacred field and proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on jihai the emperor plowed the sacred field and issued a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 二月，魏司空東郡王陸定國坐恃恩不法，免官爵為兵。

translations.literal: In the second month, the Wei Minister of Works, Prince Lu Dingguo of Dongjun, was stripped of office and rank for relying on favor and breaking the law, and was made a common soldier.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, the Northern Wei minister of works Prince Lu Dingguo of Dongjun was stripped of office and rank for abusing imperial favor and violating the law, and reduced to common soldiery.

sentences.zh: 魏馮太后內行不正，以李弈之死怨顯祖，密行鴆毒，夏，六月，辛未，顯祖殂。

translations.literal: The Wei Empress Dowager's private conduct was improper; she harbored resentment toward Emperor Xianwen over Li Yi's death and secretly administered poison. In summer, the sixth month, on xinwei Emperor Xianwen died.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Wei empress dowager's private conduct was improper. She resented Emperor Xianwen over Li Yi's death and secretly poisoned him. In summer, the sixth month, on xinwei Emperor Xianwen died.

sentences.zh: 壬申，大赦，改元承明。

translations.literal: On renshen a general amnesty was proclaimed and the era name was changed to Chengming.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen a general amnesty was declared and the era name changed to Chengming.

sentences.zh: 葬顯祖於金陵，謚曰獻文皇帝。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianwen was buried at Jinling with the posthumous title Emperor Xianwen.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianwen was buried at Jinling with the posthumous title Emperor Xianwen.

sentences.zh: 魏大司馬、大將軍代人萬安國坐矯詔殺神部長奚買奴，賜死。

translations.literal: The Wei Grand Minister of War and Grand General Wan Anguo, a man of Dai, was sentenced to death for forging an edict to kill Xi Mainu, head of the Shen tribe.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Wei grand minister of war and grand general Wan Anguo, a man of Dai, was sentenced to death for forging an edict to kill Xi Mainu, chief of the Shen tribe.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，魏以征西大將軍、安樂王長樂為太尉，尚書左僕射、宜都王目辰為司徒，南部尚書李言斤為司空。

translations.literal: On wuyin the Wei appointed Grand General for Pacifying the West, Prince Changle of Anle, as Grand Minister of War; Vice-Director of the Masters of Writing, left, Prince Muchen of Yidu, as Minister of Works; and Minister in the Southern Department Li Yanjin as Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin the Northern Wei made pacification-west grand general Prince Changle of Anle grand minister of war, left vice-director of the masters of writing Prince Muchen of Yidu minister of works, and southern-department minister Li Yanjin minister of ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 尊皇太后曰太皇太后，復臨朝稱制。

translations.literal: The empress dowager was honored as grand empress dowager and again held court and exercised regency.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager was raised to grand empress dowager and again presided over court, exercising regency.

sentences.zh: 以馮熙為侍中、太師、中書監。

translations.literal: Feng Xi was appointed Attendant-in-Ordinary, Grand Preceptor, and Supervisor of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Xi was made attendant-in-ordinary, grand preceptor, and supervisor of the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 熙自以外戚，固辭內任；

translations.literal: Xi, being a maternal relative by marriage, firmly declined interior office;
translations.idiomatic: Xi, as a maternal kinsman by marriage, firmly declined posts at the inner court;

sentences.zh: 乃除都督、洛州刺史，侍中、太師如故。

translations.literal: and so was instead appointed Area Commander-in-Chief and governor of Luozhou, while retaining his posts as Attendant-in-Ordinary and Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: and was instead appointed area commander-in-chief and governor of Luozhou, while keeping the titles of attendant-in-ordinary and grand preceptor.

sentences.zh: 顯祖神主祔太廟，有司奏廟中執事之官，請依故事皆賜爵。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianwen's spirit tablet was enshrined in the Ancestral Temple; the relevant offices reported that officials serving in the temple should, according to precedent, all be granted noble ranks.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xianwen's spirit tablet was placed in the ancestral temple, the relevant offices proposed that temple officials should, by precedent, all receive ennoblement.

sentences.zh: 秘書令廣平程駿上言：「建侯裂地，帝王所重，或以親賢，或因功伐，未聞神主祔廟而百司受封者也。

translations.literal: Secretary Supervisor Cheng Jun of Guangping submitted: "Establishing feudatories and dividing lands—these are what emperors value highly, whether for kinsmen and worthies or for meritorious service; one has not heard of shrine tablets being enshrined in the temple while a hundred offices receive enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: Secretary supervisor Cheng Jun of Guangping wrote: "Creating feudatories and apportioning land are acts emperors weigh heavily—sometimes for kin and worthies, sometimes for merit in conquest—but never have I heard of enfeoffing every office because a spirit tablet enters the temple.

sentences.zh: 皇家故事，蓋一時之恩，豈可為長世之法乎！」

translations.literal: Our house's precedent was surely a grant for a single occasion; how could it serve as a model for all time?"
translations.idiomatic: Our dynasty's precedent was surely a one-time grace; how could that become permanent law?"

sentences.zh: 太后善而從之，謂群臣曰：「凡議事，當依古典正言，豈得但修故事而已！」

translations.literal: The empress dowager approved and followed his advice, telling the assembled ministers: "Whenever you deliberate on affairs, you should rely on classical standards and speak correctly; how can you merely follow precedent!"
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager approved and followed his counsel, telling the assembled ministers: "Whenever you deliberate on policy, you should appeal to classical standards and speak to the point—not merely repeat old practice!"

sentences.zh: 賜駿衣一襲，帛二百匹。

translations.literal: She bestowed on Jun one suit of clothing and two hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: She rewarded Jun with one suit of robes and two hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 太后性聰察，知書計，曉政事，被服儉素，膳羞減於故事什七八；

translations.literal: The empress dowager was intelligent and perceptive, knew writing and reckoning, and understood administration; her dress was plain, and her meals were reduced by seven or eight tenths compared with former precedent;
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager was quick and perceptive, literate and skilled at calculation, and adept at government. She dressed plainly, and her table was cut by seven or eight parts in ten compared with former usage;

sentences.zh: 而猜忍多權數。

translations.literal: yet she was suspicious, harsh, and fond of stratagems.
translations.idiomatic: yet she was suspicious, cruel, and fond of political maneuver.

sentences.zh: 高祖性至孝，能承顏順志。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu was supremely filial and could comply with her expression and will.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu was profoundly filial and could match her mood and wishes.

sentences.zh: 事無大小，皆仰成於太后。

translations.literal: Affairs great and small all depended on the empress dowager's completion.
translations.idiomatic: Matters great and small all awaited the empress dowager's decision.

sentences.zh: 太后往往專決，不復關白於帝。

translations.literal: The empress dowager often decided on her own and no longer reported to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: She often decided on her own without informing the emperor.

sentences.zh: 所幸宦者高平王琚、安定張祜、杞嶷、馮翊王遇、略陽苻承祖、高陰王質，皆依勢用事。

translations.literal: Among those she favored were the eunuchs Prince Ju of Gaoping, Zhang Hu of Anding, Qi Yi, Wang Yu of Fengyi, Fu Chengzu of Lueyang, and Wang Zhi of Gaoyin—all wielded power by her favor.
translations.idiomatic: Those in her favor included the eunuchs Prince Ju of Gaoping, Zhang Hu of Anding, Qi Yi, Wang Yu of Fengyi, Fu Chenzu of Lueyang, and Wang Zhi of Gaoyin—all wielded power through her patronage.

sentences.zh: 祜官至尚書左僕射，爵新平王；

translations.literal: Hu rose to Vice-Director of the Masters of Writing, left, with the title Prince of Xinping;
translations.idiomatic: Hu rose to left vice-director of the masters of writing and prince of Xinping;

sentences.zh: 琚官至征南將軍，爵高平王；

translations.literal: Ju rose to General Who Pacifies the South with the title Prince of Gaoping;
translations.idiomatic: Ju rose to general who pacifies the south and prince of Gaoping;

sentences.zh: 嶷等官亦至侍中、吏部尚書、刺史，爵為公、侯，賞賜巨萬，賜鐵券，許以不死。

translations.literal: Yi and the others also reached attendant-in-ordinary, minister in charge of the officials, and regional governor, with ranks of duke and marquis; their rewards ran to tens of thousands, and they were given iron certificates promising they would not be executed.
translations.idiomatic: Yi and the others also reached attendant-in-ordinary, minister of personnel, and provincial inspector, with ranks of duke and marquis; rewards ran into the tens of thousands, and they received iron certificates granting immunity from execution.

sentences.zh: 又，太卜令姑臧王睿得幸於太后，超遷至侍中、吏部尚書，爵太原公。

translations.literal: Moreover, the Grand Diviner Wang Rui of Guzang won the empress dowager's favor and was swiftly promoted to attendant-in-ordinary, minister in charge of the officials, and Duke of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Grand diviner Wang Rui of Guzang also won her favor and was swiftly promoted to attendant-in-ordinary, minister of personnel, and duke of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 秘書令李沖，雖以才進，亦由私寵，賞賜皆不可勝紀。

translations.literal: Secretary Supervisor Li Chong, though advanced for talent, was also advanced through private favor; his rewards were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Secretary supervisor Li Chong, though promoted on talent, owed his rise also to private favor; his rewards were beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 又外禮人望東陽王丕、游明根等，皆極其優厚，每褒賞睿等，輒以丕等參之，以示不私。

translations.literal: She likewise treated with utmost generosity men of outward reputation such as Prince Pi of Dongyang and You Minggen, richly rewarding them whenever she commended Rui and the others, always citing Pi and the like as well, to show impartiality.
translations.idiomatic: She likewise treated with the greatest generosity men of outward reputation such as Prince Pi of Dongyang and You Minggen, richly rewarding them whenever she praised Rui and the others—always naming Pi and the like as well, to show she was not partial.

sentences.zh: 丕，烈帝之玄孫；

translations.literal: Pi was a great-grandson of Emperor Lie;
translations.idiomatic: Pi was a great-grandson of Emperor Lie;

sentences.zh: 沖，寶之子也。

translations.literal: Chong was a son of Bao.
translations.idiomatic: Chong was a son of Bao.

sentences.zh: 太后自以失行，畏以議己，群下語言小涉疑忌，輒殺之。

translations.literal: The empress dowager, knowing her own misconduct, feared that others would speak of her; if subordinates' words even touched on what aroused suspicion, she put them to death.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing her own misconduct, the empress dowager feared criticism; if anyone beneath her so much as broached what aroused her suspicion, she had him killed.

sentences.zh: 然所寵幸左右，苟有小過，必加笞棰，或至百餘；

translations.literal: Yet toward those in her favor at her side, if they committed some small fault, she invariably had them caned and flogged, sometimes to more than a hundred blows;
translations.idiomatic: Yet toward favorites at her side, the smallest slip brought caning and flogging, sometimes more than a hundred strokes;

sentences.zh: 而無宿憾，尋復待之如初，或因此更富貴。

translations.literal: yet she bore no lasting resentment and soon treated them again as before, or they became even richer and more honored because of it.
translations.idiomatic: yet she bore no lasting grudge and soon treated them as before—or they grew even richer and more honored because of the beating.

sentences.zh: 故左右雖被罰，終無離心。

translations.literal: Thus though those at her side were punished, in the end they had no thought of leaving her.
translations.idiomatic: Thus though her intimates were punished, none in the end deserted her.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，加蕭道成尚書左僕射，劉秉中書令。

translations.literal: On yihai Xiao Daocheng was made Vice-Director of the Masters of Writing, left, and Liu Bing was made Master of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai Xiao Daocheng was promoted to left vice-director of the masters of writing, and Liu Bing was made master of writing.

sentences.zh: 楊運長、阮佃夫等忌建平王景素益甚，景素乃與錄事參軍陳郡殷濔、中兵參軍略陽垣慶延、參軍沈顒、左暄等謀為自全之計。

translations.literal: Yang Yunchang, Ruan Tianfu, and the others came to hate Prince Jing of Pingping ever more; Jing therefore joined with Recorder Chen Yin of Chen commandery, Headquarters Aide Yuan Qingyan of Lueyang, aide Shen Yun, and Zuo Xuan in plotting measures for self-preservation.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yunchang, Ruan Tianfu, and their faction hated Prince Jing of Pingping ever more fiercely; Jing therefore plotted with recorder Chen Yin of Chen commandery, headquarters aide Yuan Qingyan of Lueyang, aide Shen Yun, and Zuo Xuan to secure himself.

sentences.zh: 遣人往來建康，要結才力之士，冠軍將軍黃回、游擊將軍高道慶、輔國將軍曹欣之、前軍將國韓道清、長水校尉郭蘭之、羽林監垣祗祖，皆陰與通謀；

translations.literal: They sent men back and forth to Jiankang to win over men of talent and strength: Champion General Huang Hui, Mobile Corps General Gao Daoqing, Support-the-State General Cao Xinzhi, Vanguard General Han Daoqing of Guo, Chief Commandant of the Changshui Guard Guo Lanzhi, and Supervisor of the Feathered Forest Guard Yuan Qizu—all secretly communicated with them in conspiracy;
translations.idiomatic: They sent agents to and from Jiankang to recruit men of talent and force: champion general Huang Hui, mobile-corps general Gao Daoqing, support-the-state general Cao Xinzhi, vanguard general Han Daoqing of Guo, changshui chief commandant Guo Lanzhi, and feathered-forest supervisor Yuan Qizu—all secretly joined the plot;

sentences.zh: 武人不得志者，無不歸之。

translations.literal: military men who had not found favor all turned to them.
translations.idiomatic: Every frustrated military man rallied to them.

sentences.zh: 時帝好獨出遊走郊野，欣之謀據石頭城，伺帝出作亂。

translations.literal: At the time the emperor liked to go out alone to roam the suburbs and countryside; Xinzhi planned to seize Stone City and wait for the emperor to go out, then raise a disturbance.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then liked to go out alone into the suburbs; Xinzhi planned to seize Stone City and strike when the emperor left the palace.

sentences.zh: 道清、蘭之欲說蕭道成因帝夜出，執帝迎景素，道成不從者，即圖之；

translations.literal: Daoqing and Lanzhi wished to persuade Xiao Daocheng that when the emperor went out at night they should seize the emperor and welcome Jing; if Daocheng would not comply, they would plot against him;
translations.idiomatic: Daoqing and Lanzhi wanted to persuade Xiao Daocheng that when the emperor went out at night they should seize him and install Jing; if Daocheng refused, they would move against him;

sentences.zh: 景素每禁使緩之。

translations.literal: Jing always forbade them and made them hold back.
translations.idiomatic: Jing always forbade them and held them back.

sentences.zh: 楊、阮微聞其事，遣傖人周天賜偽投景素，勸令舉兵。

translations.literal: Yang and Ruan caught faint word of the affair and sent the bondservant Zhou Tiansi to feign defection to Jing and urge him to raise troops.
translations.idiomatic: Yang and Ruan caught wind of the plot and sent the bondservant Zhou Tiansi to feign defection to Jing and urge him to rebel.

sentences.zh: 景素知之，斬天賜首送台。

translations.literal: Jing learned of it, beheaded Tiansi, and sent the head to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Jing saw through the ruse, beheaded Tiansi, and sent his head to the capital.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，祗祖帥數百人自建康奔京口，雲京師已潰亂，勸令速入。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Qizu led several hundred men from Jiankang in flight to Jingkou, reporting that the capital had already collapsed in disorder and urging Jing to enter quickly.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, Qizu fled Jiankang for Jingkou at the head of several hundred men, claiming the capital had already fallen into chaos and urging Jing to march in at once.

sentences.zh: 景素信之，戊子，據京口起兵，士民赴之者以千數。

translations.literal: Jing believed him; on wuzi he seized Jingkou and raised troops, and gentry and commoners who came to join him numbered in the thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Jing believed him. On wuzi he seized Jingkou and raised the standard; thousands of gentry and commoners rallied to him.

sentences.zh: 楊、阮聞祗祖叛走，即命纂嚴。

translations.literal: When Yang and Ruan heard that Qizu had rebelled and fled, they immediately ordered the tightening of defenses.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang and Ruan heard Qizu had rebelled and fled, they immediately ordered a general mobilization.

sentences.zh: 己丑，遣驍騎將軍任農夫、領軍將軍黃回、左軍將軍蘭陵李安民將步軍，右軍將軍張保將水軍，以討之；

translations.literal: On jichou they sent Valiant Cavalry General Ren Nongfu, Army Inspector Huang Hui, and Left Army General Li Anmin of Lanling to command the infantry, and Right Army General Zhang Bao to command the navy, to attack him;
translations.idiomatic: On jichou they dispatched valiant-cavalry general Ren Nongfu, army inspector Huang Hui, and left-army general Li Anmin of Lanling with the infantry, and right-army general Zhang Bao with the fleet, to suppress him;

sentences.zh: 辛卯，又命南豫州刺史段佛榮為都統。

translations.literal: On xinmao they further appointed Duan Furong, governor of South Yuzhou, as overall commander.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao they further named Duan Furong, governor of South Yuzhou, supreme commander.

sentences.zh: 蕭道成知黃回有異志，故使安民、佛榮與之偕行。

translations.literal: Xiao Daocheng knew Huang Hui harbored a different intent, and therefore had Anmin and Furong march with him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Daocheng knew Huang Hui was disloyal, and therefore sent Anmin and Furong along with him.

sentences.zh: 回私戒其士卒：「道逢京口兵，勿得戰。」

translations.literal: Hui privately warned his troops: "If you meet Jingkou troops on the road, you must not fight."
translations.idiomatic: Hui secretly ordered his men: "If you meet Jingkou troops on the march, do not engage."

sentences.zh: 道成屯玄武湖，冠軍將軍蕭賾鎮東府。

translations.literal: Daocheng encamped at Black Tortoise Lake; Champion General Xiao Ze guarded the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Daocheng encamped at Black Tortoise Lake while champion general Xiao Ze held the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 始安王伯融，都鄉侯伯猷，皆建安王休仁之子也，楊、阮忌其年長，悉稱詔賜死。

translations.literal: Prince Borong of Shi'an and Marquis Boyou of Duxiang were both sons of Prince Jian'an Xiuren; Yang and Ruan, jealous of their advancing years, all had them put to death by imperial order in name.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Borong of Shi'an and Marquis Boyou of Duxiang were both sons of Prince Jian'an Xiuren. Yang and Ruan, fearing their maturity, had them all put to death by forged edict.

sentences.zh: 景素欲斷竹裡以拒台軍。

translations.literal: Jing wished to cut down the bamboo groves to block the imperial army.
translations.idiomatic: Jing wanted to clear the bamboo groves to block the imperial army.

sentences.zh: 垣慶延、垣祗祖、沈顒皆曰：「今天時旱熱，台軍遠來疲睏，引之使至，以逸待勞，可一戰而克。」

translations.literal: Yuan Qingyan, Yuan Qizu, and Shen Yun all said: "Now the season is hot and dry; the imperial army has come from afar and is weary. Draw them on until they arrive, then meet their labor with your ease—you can overcome them in a single battle."
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Qingyan, Qizu, and Shen Yun all said: "The weather is blazing; the imperial army has marched far and is exhausted. Let them come to us and fight fresh against weary men—we can break them in one battle."

sentences.zh: 殷濔等固爭，不能得。

translations.literal: Chen Yin and the others argued firmly but could not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yin and the others argued fiercely but could not prevail.

sentences.zh: 農夫等既至，縱火燒市邑。

translations.literal: When Nongfu and the others arrived, they set fire and burned the market towns.
translations.idiomatic: When Nongfu and the others arrived, they set the market towns ablaze.

sentences.zh: 慶延等各相顧望，莫有鬥志；

translations.literal: Qingyan and the others looked at one another and none had fighting spirit;
translations.idiomatic: Qingyan and the others exchanged glances; none had the will to fight;

sentences.zh: 景素本乏威略，恇擾不知所為。

translations.literal: Jing had always lacked authority and strategy, and in fear and confusion did not know what to do.
translations.idiomatic: Jing had never possessed authority or strategy; in panic he did not know what to do.

sentences.zh: 黃回迫於段佛榮，且見京口軍弱，遂不發。

translations.literal: Huang Hui, pressed by Duan Furong and seeing the Jingkou army was weak, therefore did not act.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Hui, constrained by Duan Furong and seeing how weak the Jingkou force was, held back and did not move.

sentences.zh: 張保泊西渚，景素左右勇士數十人，自相要結，進擊水軍。

translations.literal: Zhang Bao moored at the western ford; several dozen brave warriors at Jing's side bound themselves together by oath and advanced to attack the navy.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Bao anchored at the western ford. Several dozen of Jing's bravest followers swore a pact and attacked the fleet.

sentences.zh: 甲午，張保敗死，而諸將不相應赴，復為台軍所破。

translations.literal: On jiawu Zhang Bao was defeated and killed, yet the generals did not support one another in going to his aid, and were again broken by the imperial army.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu Zhang Bao was defeated and killed, but the other generals failed to support him and were routed again by the imperial army.

sentences.zh: 台軍既薄城下，顒先帥眾走，祗祖次之，其餘諸軍相繼奔退，獨左暄與台軍力戰於萬歲樓下；

translations.literal: Once the imperial army had pressed to the foot of the walls, Yun was first to lead his troops in flight, Qizu next, and the rest of the armies successively fled; only Zuo Xuan fought the imperial army fiercely below the Tower of Ten Thousand Years;
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial army reached the walls, Yun was first to flee with his men, then Qizu, then the rest in succession; only Zuo Xuan fought the imperial troops fiercely below the Tower of Ten Thousand Years;

sentences.zh: 而所配兵力甚弱，不能敵而散。

translations.literal: but the force assigned him was very weak and could not resist, so they scattered.
translations.idiomatic: but his detachment was too weak to hold and broke apart.

sentences.zh: 乙未，拔京口。

translations.literal: On yiwei they stormed and took Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei they stormed and took Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 黃回軍先入，自以有誓不殺諸王，乃以景素讓殿中將軍張倪奴。

translations.literal: Huang Hui's army entered first; he considered himself bound by an oath not to kill princes, and therefore handed Jing over to Palace Attendant Zhang Ninu.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Hui's troops entered first. Bound by an oath not to kill princes, he handed Jing over to palace attendant Zhang Ninu.

sentences.zh: 倪奴擒景素，斬之，並其三子，同黨垣祗祖等數十人皆伏誅。

translations.literal: Ninu seized Jing and beheaded him, together with his three sons; several dozen co-conspirators including Yuan Qizu were all executed.
translations.idiomatic: Ninu seized Jing and beheaded him along with his three sons; several dozen accomplices including Qizu were all executed.

sentences.zh: 蕭道成釋黃回、高道慶不問，撫之如舊。

translations.literal: Xiao Daocheng released Huang Hui and Gao Daoqing without inquiry and treated them as before.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Daocheng released Huang Hui and Gao Daoqing without punishment and treated them as before.

sentences.zh: 是日，解嚴。

translations.literal: That day the tightened defenses were lifted.
translations.idiomatic: That day the mobilization was lifted.

sentences.zh: 丙申，大赦。

translations.literal: On bingshen a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen a general amnesty was declared.

sentences.zh: 初，巴東建平蠻反，沈攸之遣軍討之。

translations.literal: Earlier, the barbarians of Badong and Jianping had rebelled, and Shen Youzhi had sent troops to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the tribes of Badong and Jianping had rebelled, and Shen Youzhi had sent troops to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 及景素反，攸之急追峽中軍以赴建康。

translations.literal: When Jing rebelled, Youzhi urgently pursued the army in the gorges to hurry to Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing rebelled, Youzhi urgently recalled his gorge army to march on Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 巴東太守劉攘兵、建平太守劉道欣疑攸之有異謀，勒兵斷峽，不聽軍下。

translations.literal: Liu Rangbing, governor of Badong, and Liu Daoxin, governor of Jianping, suspected Youzhi of a different plot and led troops to block the gorges, not permitting the army to descend.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Rangbing, governor of Badong, and Liu Daoxin, governor of Jianping, suspected Youzhi of ulterior designs and blocked the gorges with troops, refusing to let his army pass downstream.

sentences.zh: 攘兵子天賜為荊州西曹，攸之遣天賜往諭之。

translations.literal: Rangbing's son Tiansi was Western Aide of Jingzhou; Youzhi sent Tiansi to instruct them.
translations.idiomatic: Rangbing's son Tiansi served as western aide of Jingzhou; Youzhi sent Tiansi to reason with them.

sentences.zh: 攘兵知景素實反，乃釋甲謝愆，攸之待之如故。

translations.literal: Rangbing learned that Jing had in fact rebelled, then laid down arms and acknowledged his fault; Youzhi treated him as before.
translations.idiomatic: Once Rangbing learned Jing had truly rebelled, he laid down arms and apologized; Youzhi treated him as before.

sentences.zh: 劉道欣堅守建平，攘兵譬說不回，乃與伐蠻軍攻斬之。

translations.literal: Liu Daoxin held Jianping firmly; Rangbing exhorted him but could not turn him, and so joined the army suppressing the barbarians in attacking and beheading him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Daoxin held firm at Jianping. Rangbing pleaded with him in vain, then joined the anti-tribal force in attacking and killing him.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，魏主追尊其母李貴人曰思皇后。

translations.literal: On jiachen the Wei ruler posthumously honored his mother, Lady Li, as Empress Si.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen the Northern Wei emperor posthumously honored his mother Lady Li as Empress Si.

sentences.zh: 八月，丁卯，立皇弟翽為南陽王，嵩為新興王，禧為始建王。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on dingmao, the emperor's younger brothers Hui, Song, and Xi were established as Prince of Nanyang, Prince of Xinxing, and Prince of Shijian respectively.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on dingmao, the emperor enfeoffed his younger brothers Hui as prince of Nanyang, Song as prince of Xinxing, and Xi as prince of Shijian.

sentences.zh: 庚午，以給事黃門侍郎阮佃夫為南豫州刺史，留鎮京師。

translations.literal: On gengwu Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Yellow Gate Ruan Tianfu was made governor of South Yuzhou, remaining to guard the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu attendant-in-ordinary of the yellow gate Ruan Tianfu was named governor of South Yuzhou while remaining to guard the capital.

sentences.zh: 九月，戊子，賜驍騎將軍道慶死。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on wuzi, Valiant Cavalry General Daoqing was sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on wuzi, valiant-cavalry general Daoqing was sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，辛酉，以吏部尚書王僧虔為尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on xinyou, Wang Sengqian, minister in charge of the officials, was made Vice-Director of the Masters of Writing, right.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on xinyou, minister of personnel Wang Sengqian was made right vice-director of the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 十一月，戊子，魏以太尉、安樂王長樂為定州刺史，司空李言斤為徐州刺史。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on wuzi, the Wei made Grand Minister of War Prince Changle of Anle governor of Dingzhou and Minister of Ceremonies Li Yanjin governor of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on wuzi, the Northern Wei appointed grand minister of war Prince Changle of Anle governor of Dingzhou and minister of ceremonies Li Yanjin governor of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 順皇帝

translations.literal: The Deposed Emperor
translations.idiomatic: The Deposed Emperor

sentences.zh: 蒼梧王下升明元年（

translations.literal: Deposed Emperor of Cangwu, lower scroll, Shengming year 1 (
translations.idiomatic: Deposed Emperor of Cangwu, lower scroll, Shengming year 1 (

sentences.zh: 丁巳，公元四七七年）

translations.literal: dingsi, 477 CE)
translations.idiomatic: dingsi, AD 477)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，乙酉朔，魏改元太和。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on the yiyou new moon, the Wei changed the era name to Taihe.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on the yiyou new moon, the Northern Wei changed the era name to Taihe.

sentences.zh: 己酉，略陽氐王元壽聚眾五千餘家，自稱沖天王；

translations.literal: On jiyou the Di king Yuan Shou of Lueyang gathered more than five thousand households and styled himself the Heaven-Storming King;
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou the Di king Yuan Shou of Lueyang rallied more than five thousand households and proclaimed himself the Heaven-Storming King;

sentences.zh: 二月，辛未，魏秦、益二州刺史尉洛侯擊破之。

translations.literal: in the second month, on xinwei, Wei governors of Qin and Yi provinces Wei Luohou defeated and broke him.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on xinwei, the Northern Wei governors of Qin and Yi Wei Luohou defeated and routed him.

sentences.zh: 三月，庚子，魏以東陽王丕為司徒。

translations.literal: In the third month, on gengzi, the Wei made Prince Pi of Dongyang Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on gengzi, the Northern Wei made Prince Pi of Dongyang minister of works.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，丁卯，魏主如白登；

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on dingmao, the Wei ruler went to Baideng;
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on dingmao, the Northern Wei emperor went to Baideng;

sentences.zh: 壬申，如崞山。

translations.literal: on renshen he went to Guo Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: on renshen he went to Guo Mountain.

sentences.zh: 初，蒼梧王在東宮，好緣漆帳竿，去地丈餘；

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Deposed Emperor of Cangwu was in the Eastern Palace, he liked to climb lacquered curtain poles more than ten feet above the ground;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while still in the Eastern Palace, the future deposed emperor liked to climb lacquered curtain poles more than ten feet off the ground;

sentences.zh: 喜怒乖節，主帥不能禁。

translations.literal: his joy and anger were contrary to propriety, and the palace stewards could not restrain him.
translations.idiomatic: his moods swung wildly beyond all propriety, and the palace stewards could not restrain him.

sentences.zh: 太宗屢敕陳太妃痛捶之。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong repeatedly ordered Consort Chen to beat him severely.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong repeatedly ordered Consort Chen to beat him severely.

sentences.zh: 及即帝位，內畏太后、太妃，外憚諸大臣，未敢縱逸。

translations.literal: When he ascended the throne, inwardly he feared the empress dowager and the consort dowager, and outwardly he stood in awe of the great ministers, and did not yet dare to indulge himself.
translations.idiomatic: When he took the throne he still feared the empress dowager and consort dowager within and the great ministers without, and did not yet dare to run wild.

sentences.zh: 自加元服，內外稍無以制，數出遊行。

translations.literal: From the time he received the capping ceremony, within and without there was gradually no one who could control him, and he often went out roaming.
translations.idiomatic: After his capping ceremony no one inside or outside court could restrain him, and he went out roaming again and again.

sentences.zh: 始出宮，猶整儀衛。

translations.literal: At first when he left the palace he still kept his guard of honor in order.
translations.idiomatic: At first when he left the palace he still kept a proper guard of honor.

sentences.zh: 俄而棄車騎，帥左右數人，或出郊野，或入市廛。

translations.literal: Before long he abandoned chariots and escort, leading a few attendants, sometimes going out to the suburbs and countryside, sometimes entering the markets.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he abandoned his carriage and escort, taking only a few attendants—sometimes into the suburbs, sometimes into the markets.

sentences.zh: 太妃每乘青犢車，隨相檢攝。

translations.literal: The consort dowager would each time ride in a green ox-cart and follow to supervise and restrain him.
translations.idiomatic: The consort dowager would follow in a green ox-cart to keep watch on him.

sentences.zh: 既而輕騎遠走一二十里，太妃不復能追；

translations.literal: before long he would gallop lightly ten or twenty li away, and the consort dowager could no longer catch up;
translations.idiomatic: Before long he would ride off ten or twenty li, and she could no longer catch up;

sentences.zh: 儀衛亦懼禍不敢追尋，唯整部伍，別在一處，瞻望而已。

translations.literal: the guard of honor also feared disaster and dared not pursue, only keeping their ranks formed and standing apart in another place, gazing from afar.
translations.idiomatic: the guard of honor also feared for their lives and dared not pursue, only holding formation at a distance and watching.

sentences.zh: 初，太宗嘗以陳太妃賜嬖人李道兒，已復迎還，生帝。

translations.literal: Earlier, Emperor Taizong had once given Consort Chen to his favorite Li Dao'er, then welcomed her back again; she bore the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Emperor Taizong had once given Consort Chen to his favorite Li Dao'er, then taken her back; she bore the emperor.

sentences.zh: 故帝每微行，自稱「劉統」，或稱「李將軍」。

translations.literal: Therefore when the emperor went out incognito he called himself "Liu Tong," or styled himself "General Li."
translations.idiomatic: When he went out incognito he called himself "Liu Tong" or "General Li."

sentences.zh: 常著小褲衫，營署巷陌，無不貫穿；

translations.literal: He often wore short trousers and a shirt, and there was no barracks, lane, or alley he did not pass through;
translations.idiomatic: He often wore only short trousers and a shirt, roaming every barracks, lane, and alley;

sentences.zh: 或夜宿客舍，或晝臥道旁，排突廝養，與之交易，或遭慢辱，悅而受之。

translations.literal: sometimes sleeping at an inn by night, sometimes lying by the roadside by day, shouldering aside grooms and servants, trading with them, or suffering insult and taking pleasure in accepting it.
translations.idiomatic: sometimes sleeping in inns at night, sometimes napping by the roadside by day, shoving aside servants and haggling with them—he even enjoyed being insulted.

sentences.zh: 凡諸鄙事，裁衣、作帽，過目則能；

translations.literal: in all vulgar crafts—cutting clothes, making hats—once he saw them he could do them;
translations.idiomatic: In every vulgar craft—cutting clothes, making hats—he could do whatever he saw once;

sentences.zh: 未嘗吹篪，執管便韻。

translations.literal: he had never blown the chi, yet taking the pipe he at once produced melody.
translations.idiomatic: he had never played the chi, yet the moment he took up a pipe he produced melody.

sentences.zh: 及京口既平，驕恣尤甚，無日不出，夕去晨返，晨出暮歸。

translations.literal: After Jingkou was pacified his arrogance and license grew extreme; not a day passed without his going out—leaving at evening and returning at dawn, or leaving at dawn and returning at evening.
translations.idiomatic: After Jingkou was pacified his arrogance knew no bounds. He went out every day—sometimes leaving at dusk and returning at dawn, sometimes leaving at dawn and returning at nightfall.

sentences.zh: 從者並執金延矛，行人男女及犬馬牛驢，逢無免者。

translations.literal: His followers all bore gilded spears with extended shafts; men and women on the road, and dogs, horses, cattle, and donkeys—none who met them escaped.
translations.idiomatic: His followers carried gilded spears; no man, woman, dog, horse, ox, or donkey they met was spared.

sentences.zh: 民間擾懼，商販皆息，門戶晝閉，行人殆絕。

translations.literal: The common people were disturbed and fearful; merchants all ceased trade; doors were shut by day; travelers nearly vanished.
translations.idiomatic: The people lived in terror. Commerce ceased, doors stayed shut by day, and travelers nearly disappeared from the roads.

sentences.zh: 針、椎、鑿、鋸，不離左右，小有忤意，即加屠剖，一日不殺，則慘然不樂；

translations.literal: Needles, awls, chisels, and saws never left his side; at the slightest offense he at once butchered and dismembered; if he did not kill for a day, he was gloomily unhappy;
translations.idiomatic: Needles, awls, chisels, and saws never left his side. The slightest provocation brought butchery and dismemberment; if he went a day without killing, he grew despondent;

sentences.zh: 殿省憂惶，食息不保。

translations.literal: the palace offices were anxious and fearful, unable to secure their meals and breath.
translations.idiomatic: the palace staff lived in dread, never sure they would see the next meal.

sentences.zh: 阮佃夫與直閣將軍申伯宗等謀因帝出江乘射雉，稱太后令，喚隊仗還，閉城門，遣人執帝廢之，立安成王准。

translations.literal: Ruan Tianfu and Palace Attendant General Shen Bozong and others plotted that when the emperor went to Jiangcheng to hunt pheasants, they would claim the empress dowager's order, summon the guard units back, shut the city gates, send men to seize the emperor and depose him, and establish Prince Zhun of Ancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Ruan Tianfu and palace attendant general Shen Bozong plotted to wait until the emperor went to Jiangcheng to hunt pheasants, then claim an order from the empress dowager, recall the guard units, shut the gates, seize the emperor, depose him, and install Prince Zhun of Ancheng.

sentences.zh: 事覺，甲戌，帝收佃夫等殺之。

translations.literal: The affair was discovered; on jiaxu the emperor arrested Tianfu and the others and killed them.
translations.idiomatic: The plot was discovered. On jiaxu the emperor arrested Tianfu and his co-conspirators and executed them.

sentences.zh: 太后數訓戒帝，帝不悅。

translations.literal: The empress dowager repeatedly admonished and warned the emperor; the emperor was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager repeatedly admonished him; he was displeased.

sentences.zh: 會端午，太后賜帝毛扇。

translations.literal: It happened to be the Dragon Boat Festival; the empress dowager gave the emperor a feather fan.
translations.idiomatic: At the Dragon Boat Festival the empress dowager gave him a feather fan.

sentences.zh: 帝嫌其不華，令太醫煮藥，欲鴆太后。

translations.literal: The emperor thought it insufficiently splendid and ordered the imperial physician to brew medicine, intending to poison the empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: Finding it too plain, he ordered the imperial physician to brew poison intended for the empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 左右止之曰：「若行此事，官便應作孝子，豈復得出入狡獪！」

translations.literal: Those at his side stopped him, saying: "If you do this, Your Majesty would have to act the filial son—how could you still go out roaming as you please!"
translations.idiomatic: His attendants stopped him: "If you do that, you would have to play the filial son—how could you still roam the streets as you please?"

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「汝語大有理！」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Your words make excellent sense!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "You make excellent sense!"

sentences.zh: 乃止。

translations.literal: and so he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: And he dropped the plan.

sentences.zh: 六月，甲戌，有告散騎常侍杜幼文、司徒左長史沈勃、游擊將軍孫超之與阮佃夫同謀者，帝登帥衛士，自掩三家，悉誅之，刳解臠割，嬰孩不免。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on jiaxu, someone reported that Regular Attendant Du Youwen, Left Chief Clerk of the Minister of Works Shen Bo, and Mobile Corps General Sun Chaozhi had conspired with Ruan Tianfu; the emperor led guards in person, raided the three households himself, executed them all, disemboweled and carved them into pieces—even infants were not spared.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on jiaxu, someone reported that regular attendant Du Youwen, left chief clerk of the minister of works Shen Bo, and mobile-corps general Sun Chaozhi had conspired with Ruan Tianfu. The emperor led the guards himself, raided all three households, and slaughtered everyone—disemboweling and carving them into pieces, infants included.

sentences.zh: 沈勃時居喪在廬，左右未至，帝揮刀獨前。

translations.literal: Shen Bo was then in mourning lodge; his attendants had not yet arrived; the emperor waved his blade and advanced alone.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Bo was in his mourning lodge; before his attendants could arrive the emperor charged in alone, blade in hand.

sentences.zh: 勃知不免，手搏帝耳，唾罵之曰：「汝罪逾桀、紂，屠戮無日。」

translations.literal: Bo knew he could not escape; he seized the emperor's ear with his hand, spat on him, and cursed: "Your crimes surpass Jie and Zhou—the day of your slaughter will not be long."
translations.idiomatic: Bo knew he was doomed. He grabbed the emperor's ear, spat on him, and cursed: "Your crimes surpass Jie and Zhou of old—your day of slaughter will come soon."

sentences.zh: 遂死。

translations.literal: and so he died.
translations.idiomatic: Then he was killed.

sentences.zh: 是日，大赦。

translations.literal: That day a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: That day a general amnesty was declared.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗直入領軍府。

translations.literal: The emperor once entered the Army Inspector's headquarters directly.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once walked straight into the army inspector's headquarters.

sentences.zh: 時盛熱，蕭道成晝臥裸袒。

translations.literal: It was intensely hot; Xiao Daocheng was sleeping by day naked to the waist.
translations.idiomatic: It was sweltering; Xiao Daocheng was napping bare to the waist.

sentences.zh: 帝立道成於室內，畫腹為的，自引滿，將射之。

translations.literal: The emperor made Daocheng stand in the room, drew a target on his belly, drew the bow to the full himself, and was about to shoot him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor made Daocheng stand in the room, marked a target on his belly, drew his bow to the full, and prepared to shoot.

sentences.zh: 道成斂板曰：「老臣無罪。」

translations.literal: Daocheng gathered his tablet and said: "This old minister is without guilt."
translations.idiomatic: Daocheng clasped his tablet and said: "This old minister is innocent."

sentences.zh: 左右王天恩曰：「領軍腹大，是佳射堋；

translations.literal: Wang Tian'en at his side said: "The Army Inspector's belly is large—it is an excellent butt;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tian'en at his side said: "The army inspector's belly is huge—a perfect target;

sentences.zh: 一箭便死，後無復射；

translations.literal: one arrow and he will die, and afterward there will be nothing left to shoot;
translations.idiomatic: one arrow will kill him and you'll have nothing left to shoot;

sentences.zh: 不如以□箭射之。」

translations.literal: better to shoot him with bone-tipped arrows."
translations.idiomatic: better use bone-tipped arrows instead."

sentences.zh: 帝乃更以□箭射，正中其臍。

translations.literal: The emperor then changed to bone-tipped arrows and shot, hitting the navel squarely.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor switched to bone-tipped arrows and hit the navel dead center.

sentences.zh: 投弓大笑曰：「此手何如！」

translations.literal: He cast down the bow and laughed loudly: "How is this hand!"
translations.idiomatic: He tossed down the bow and laughed: "How's that for marksmanship!"

sentences.zh: 帝忌道成威名，嘗自磨鋋，曰：「明日殺蕭道成！」

translations.literal: The emperor resented Daocheng's renown; he once sharpened a blade himself and said: "Tomorrow I will kill Xiao Daocheng!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor resented Daocheng's prestige. He once sharpened a blade himself and said: "Tomorrow I'll kill Xiao Daocheng!"

sentences.zh: 陳太妃罵之曰：「蕭道成有功於國，若害之，誰復為汝盡力邪！」

translations.literal: Consort Chen cursed him: "Xiao Daocheng has merit for the state—if you harm him, who will exert himself for you again!"
translations.idiomatic: Consort Chen scolded him: "Xiao Daocheng has served the state well—kill him and who will work for you afterward?"

sentences.zh: 帝乃止。

translations.literal: The emperor then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor relented.

sentences.zh: 道成憂懼，密與袁粲、褚淵謀廢立。

translations.literal: Daocheng was anxious and fearful and secretly plotted deposition and enthronement with Yuan Can and Chu Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Daocheng, anxious and afraid, secretly plotted deposition with Yuan Can and Chu Yuan.

sentences.zh: 粲曰：「主上幼年，微過易改。

translations.literal: Can said: "Our lord is young; small faults are easy to correct.
translations.idiomatic: Can said: "The emperor is young; minor faults can still be corrected.

sentences.zh: 伊、霍之事，非季世所行；

translations.literal: The acts of Yi Yin and Huo Guang are not what a decadent age should undertake;
translations.idiomatic: What Yi Yin and Huo Guang did is not for a decadent age;

sentences.zh: 縱使功成，亦終無全地。」

translations.literal: even if it succeeded, in the end there would be no safe ground."
translations.idiomatic: even if it succeeded, you would not survive unscathed."

sentences.zh: 淵默然。

translations.literal: Yuan was silent.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Yuan said nothing.

sentences.zh: 領軍功曹丹陽紀僧真言於道成曰：「今朝廷猖狂，人不自保；

translations.literal: Army Inspector Aide Ji Sengzhen of Danyang said to Daocheng: "Now the court is reckless and violent; no one can protect himself;
translations.idiomatic: Army inspector aide Ji Sengzhen of Danyang told Daocheng: "The court has gone mad; no one is safe;

sentences.zh: 天下之望，不在袁、褚，明公豈得坐受夷滅！

translations.literal: the hope of the realm is not with Yuan and Chu—how can you, my lord, sit and accept extermination!
translations.idiomatic: the realm looks not to Yuan and Chu—how can you sit still and wait to be destroyed?

sentences.zh: 存亡之機，仰希熟慮。」

translations.literal: The moment of survival or destruction—I look up hoping you will consider it thoroughly."
translations.idiomatic: Life or death hangs on this—I beg you to think it through."

sentences.zh: 道成然之。

translations.literal: Daocheng agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Daocheng agreed.

sentences.zh: 或勸道成奔廣陵起兵。

translations.literal: Some urged Daocheng to flee to Guangling and raise troops.
translations.idiomatic: Some urged Daocheng to flee to Guangling and raise an army.

sentences.zh: 道成世子賾，時為晉熙王長史，行郢州事，欲使賾將郢州兵東下會京口。

translations.literal: Daocheng's heir Ze was then chief clerk to Prince of Jinxi and acting for Yingzhou; Daocheng wished Ze to lead Yingzhou troops east to join at Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: Daocheng's heir Ze was chief clerk to Prince Jinxi and acting governor of Yingzhou; Daocheng wanted Ze to march Yingzhou troops east to Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 道成密遣所親劉僧副告其從兄行青、冀二州刺史劉善明曰：「人多見勸北固廣陵，恐未為長算。

translations.literal: Daocheng secretly sent his close associate Liu Sengfu to tell his cousin Liu Shanming, acting governor of Qing and Ji provinces: "Many have urged me to fortify Beigu and Guangling, but I fear that may not be a lasting plan.
translations.idiomatic: Daocheng secretly sent his confidant Liu Sengfu to his cousin Liu Shanming, acting governor of Qing and Ji: "Many urge me to hold Beigu and Guangling, but I doubt that is the wise course.

sentences.zh: 今秋風行起，卿若能與垣東海微共動虜，則我諸計可立。」

translations.literal: Now as the autumn winds rise, if you can stir the barbarians slightly together with Yuan Rongzu of Donghai, then my various plans can succeed."
translations.idiomatic: When the autumn winds rise, if you and Yuan Rongzu of Donghai can stir the northern barbarians even slightly, my plans can succeed."

sentences.zh: 亦告東海太守垣榮祖。

translations.literal: He also told Yuan Rongzu, governor of Donghai.
translations.idiomatic: He told the same to Yuan Rongzu, governor of Donghai.

sentences.zh: 善明曰：「宋氏將亡，愚智共知，北虜苦動，反為公患。

translations.literal: Shanming said: "The house of Song is about to perish—fool and wise alike know it—but stirring the northern barbarians with difficulty will instead become a calamity for you.
translations.idiomatic: Shanming replied: "Everyone knows the Song house is dying—but provoking the northern barbarians would only create trouble for you.

sentences.zh: 公神武高世，唯當靜以待之，因機奮發，功業自定，不可遠去根本，自貽猖蹶。」

translations.literal: Your divine martial prowess towers above the age; you should only wait quietly, then strike when the moment comes—your achievement will settle itself. You must not leave your foundation far behind and bring ruin on yourself."
translations.idiomatic: Your talent towers above the age. Wait quietly, strike when the moment comes, and success is assured. Do not abandon your base and court disaster."

sentences.zh: 榮祖亦曰：「領府去台百步，公走，人豈不知！

translations.literal: Rongzu also said: "The Army Inspector's headquarters is a hundred paces from the capital—if you flee, will people not know!
translations.idiomatic: Rongzu added: "Your headquarters is a hundred paces from the palace—if you flee, everyone will know!

sentences.zh: 若單騎輕行，廣陵人閉門不受，公欲何之！

translations.literal: If you go alone and lightly, the people of Guangling will shut their gates and not receive you—where do you think you can go!
translations.idiomatic: Ride alone to Guangling and they will shut you out—where would you go?

sentences.zh: 公今動足下床，恐即有叩台門者，公事去矣。」

translations.literal: If you now move your foot off the bed, I fear someone will at once knock on the capital gate—your affair is finished."
translations.idiomatic: Step off your bed and someone will knock on the palace gate—your cause is finished."

sentences.zh: 紀僧真曰：「主上雖無道，國家累世之基猶為安固。

translations.literal: Ji Sengzhen said: "Though our lord is without the Way, the state's foundation built over many generations is still secure.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Sengzhen said: "Though the emperor is wicked, the state's foundations built over generations still hold.

sentences.zh: 公百口，北度必不得俱。

translations.literal: Your household of a hundred mouths—if you cross north you surely cannot take them all.
translations.idiomatic: Your household of a hundred souls—you cannot take them all north.

sentences.zh: 縱得廣陵城，天子居深宮，施號令，目公為逆，何以避之！

translations.literal: Even if you took Guangling city, the Son of Heaven dwells deep in the palace, issues commands, and brands you a rebel—how would you escape that!
translations.idiomatic: Even if you took Guangling, the emperor sits in the deep palace issuing orders and branding you a rebel—how would you escape that?

sentences.zh: 此非萬全策也。」

translations.literal: This is not a plan of complete security."
translations.idiomatic: This is no sure plan."

sentences.zh: 道成族弟鎮軍長史順之及次子驃騎從事中郎嶷，皆以為：「帝好單行道路，於此立計，易以成功；

translations.literal: Daocheng's clansman, chief clerk to the Pacification Army Shunzhi, and his second son, attendant gentleman of the Valiant Cavalry Nie, both held: "The emperor likes to travel the roads alone—if you plan on this basis, success is easy;
translations.idiomatic: Daocheng's kinsman Shunzhi, chief clerk of the pacification army, and his second son Nie, attendant of the valiant cavalry, both argued: "The emperor loves to roam alone—plot on that basis and success is easy;

sentences.zh: 外州起兵，鮮有克捷，徒先人受禍耳。」

translations.literal: raising troops from outer provinces rarely wins victory—it only brings disaster on your kin first."
translations.idiomatic: raising troops in the provinces rarely succeeds—it only gets your family killed first."

sentences.zh: 道成乃止。

translations.literal: Daocheng then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Daocheng abandoned the plan.

sentences.zh: 東中郎司馬、行會稽郡事李安民欲奉江夏王躋起兵於東方，道成止之。

translations.literal: Eastern Gentlemen-Commandant Aide Li Anmin, acting for Kuaiji commandery, wished to support Prince Ji of Jiangxia in raising troops in the east; Daocheng stopped him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Anmin, eastern gentlemen-commandant aide acting for Kuaiji, wanted to raise troops in the east behind Prince Ji of Jiangxia; Daocheng stopped him.

sentences.zh: 越騎校尉王敬則潛自結於道成，夜著青衣，扶匐道路，為道成聽察帝之往來。

translations.literal: Chief Commandant of the Yue Cavalry Wang Jingze secretly attached himself to Daocheng; by night he wore green clothes and crept along the roads on hands and knees, spying for Daocheng on the emperor's comings and goings.
translations.idiomatic: Yue-cavalry chief commandant Wang Jingze secretly allied with Daocheng. By night he wore plain green clothes and crawled along the roads to report the emperor's movements.

sentences.zh: 道成命敬則陰結帝左右楊玉夫、楊萬年、陳奉伯等一十五人，於殿中詗伺機便。

translations.literal: Daocheng ordered Jingze secretly to win over fifteen men at the emperor's side including Yang Yufu, Yang Wannian, and Chen Fengbo, to watch in the palace halls for an opportunity.
translations.idiomatic: Daocheng had Jingze secretly recruit fifteen of the emperor's attendants—including Yang Yufu, Yang Wannian, and Chen Fengbo—to watch for a chance inside the palace.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，丁亥夜，帝微行至領軍府門。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on the night of dinghai, the emperor went incognito to the gate of the Army Inspector's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on the night of dinghai, the emperor went incognito to the army inspector's gate.

sentences.zh: 左右曰：「一府皆眠，何不緣牆入？」

translations.literal: Those at his side said: "The whole headquarters is asleep—why not climb the wall and enter?"
translations.idiomatic: His attendants said: "The whole compound is asleep—why not climb the wall?"

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「我今夕欲於一處作適，宜待明夕。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Tonight I wish to sport in one place; better wait until tomorrow night."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Tonight I have sport planned elsewhere—better come back tomorrow night."

sentences.zh: 員外郎桓康等於道成門間聽聞之。

translations.literal: Outer Gentleman Huan Kang and others at Daocheng's gate overheard it.
translations.idiomatic: Outer gentleman Huan Kang and others at Daocheng's gate overheard him.

sentences.zh: 戊子，帝乘露車，與左右於台岡賭跳。

translations.literal: On wuzi the emperor rode an open carriage and with his attendants wagered on leaping at Terrace Mound.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi the emperor rode an open carriage and wagered with his attendants on leaping games at Terrace Mound.

sentences.zh: 仍往青園尼寺，晚，至新安寺偷狗，就曇度道人煮之。

translations.literal: He then went to Green Garden Nunnery; in the evening he reached Xin'an Temple, stole a dog, and had the Daoist priest Tandu boil it.
translations.idiomatic: He visited Green Garden Nunnery, then in the evening stole a dog at Xin'an Temple and had the Daoist priest Tandu cook it.

sentences.zh: 飲酒醉，還仁壽殿寢。

translations.literal: He drank wine until drunk and returned to sleep in Benevolence and Longevity Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He drank himself drunk and returned to Benevolence and Longevity Hall to sleep.

sentences.zh: 楊玉夫常得帝意，至是忽憎之，見輒切齒曰：「明日當殺小子，取肝肺！」

translations.literal: Yang Yufu had often won the emperor's favor, but now the emperor suddenly hated him; whenever he saw him he ground his teeth and said: "Tomorrow I shall kill the little wretch and take his liver and lungs!"
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yufu had long been a favorite, but now the emperor suddenly hated him and would snarl whenever he saw him: "Tomorrow I'll kill the little wretch and take his liver and lungs!"

sentences.zh: 是夜，令玉夫伺織女度河，曰：「見當報我；

translations.literal: That night he ordered Yufu to watch for the Weaver Maid crossing the river, saying: "When you see it, report to me;
translations.idiomatic: That night he ordered Yufu to watch for the Weaver Maid crossing the Milky Way: "Tell me when you see it;

sentences.zh: 不見，將殺汝！」

translations.literal: if you do not see it, I will kill you!"
translations.idiomatic: if you don't, I'll kill you!"

sentences.zh: 時帝出入無常，省內諸閣，夜皆不閉，廂下畏相逢值，無敢出者；

translations.literal: At the time the emperor's comings and goings were irregular; within the palace all pavilions at night were left unshut; those in the side chambers feared meeting him by chance and none dared go out;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor came and went at random; palace gates stayed open at night; attendants in the side chambers feared meeting him and dared not venture out;

sentences.zh: 宿衛並逃避，內外莫相禁攝。

translations.literal: the night guards all fled; within and without no one restrained one another.
translations.idiomatic: night guards fled; inside and out no one kept order.

sentences.zh: 是夕，王敬則出外。

translations.literal: That evening Wang Jingze went out.
translations.idiomatic: That evening Wang Jingze went out.

sentences.zh: 玉夫伺帝熟寢，與楊萬年取帝防身刀刎之。

translations.literal: Yufu waited until the emperor slept soundly, then with Yang Wannian took the emperor's personal blade and cut his throat.
translations.idiomatic: Yufu waited until the emperor slept soundly, then he and Yang Wannian took the emperor's own blade and cut his throat.

sentences.zh: 敕廂下奏伎陳奉伯袖其首，依常行法，稱敕開承明門出，以首與敬則。

translations.literal: He ordered musicians in the side chambers; Chen Fengbo hid the head in his sleeve; following the usual procedure they claimed an edict, opened Chenming Gate, went out, and gave the head to Jingze.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the musicians in the side chambers to play. Chen Fengbo hid the head in his sleeve; following routine procedure they claimed an imperial order, opened Chenming Gate, went out, and handed the head to Jingze.

sentences.zh: 敬則馳詣領軍府，叩門大呼，蕭道成慮蒼梧王誑之，不敢開門。

translations.literal: Jingze galloped to the Army Inspector's headquarters, knocked and shouted at the gate; Xiao Daocheng feared the Deposed Emperor of Cangwu was deceiving him and dared not open.
translations.idiomatic: Jingze galloped to the army inspector's headquarters and hammered on the gate shouting. Xiao Daocheng feared a trap by the deposed emperor and would not open.

sentences.zh: 敬則於牆上投其首，道成洗視，乃戎服乘馬而出，敬則、桓康等皆從。

translations.literal: Jingze threw the head over the wall; Daocheng washed and examined it, then donned military dress, mounted a horse, and went out; Jingze, Huan Kang, and the others all followed.
translations.idiomatic: Jingze threw the head over the wall. Daocheng washed and inspected it, then donned armor, mounted, and rode out with Jingze, Huan Kang, and the rest.

sentences.zh: 入宮，至承明門，詐為行還。

translations.literal: They entered the palace, reached Chenming Gate, and pretended to be returning from an outing.
translations.idiomatic: They entered the palace, reached Chenming Gate, and pretended to be returning from a night outing.

sentences.zh: 敬則恐內人覘見，以刀環塞窐孔，呼門甚急，門開而入。

translations.literal: Jingze feared those inside would spy; he blocked the peepholes with his blade-ring, called at the gate very urgently, the gate opened, and they entered.
translations.idiomatic: Jingze feared someone inside would see; he blocked the peepholes with his sword guard, shouted urgently at the gate, and entered when it opened.

sentences.zh: 他夕，蒼梧王每開門，門者震懾，不敢仰視，至是弗之疑。

translations.literal: On other nights when the Deposed Emperor of Cangwu opened the gate, the gatekeepers were terrified and dared not look up; this time they did not suspect.
translations.idiomatic: On other nights when the deposed emperor came to the gate, guards trembled and dared not look up; this time they suspected nothing.

sentences.zh: 道成入殿，殿中驚怖。

translations.literal: Daocheng entered the hall; those in the hall were alarmed and afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Daocheng entered the hall; everyone inside was terrified.

sentences.zh: 既而聞蒼梧王死，咸稱萬歲。

translations.literal: When they then heard the Deposed Emperor of Cangwu was dead, all cried "Ten thousand years!"
translations.idiomatic: When they learned the deposed emperor was dead, all cried "Long live the emperor!"

sentences.zh: 己丑旦，道成戎服出殿庭槐樹下，以太后令召袁粲、褚淵、劉秉入會議。

translations.literal: At dawn on jichou Daocheng in military dress came out beneath the locust tree in the palace courtyard and, by the empress dowager's order, summoned Yuan Can, Chu Yuan, and Liu Bing to confer.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn on jichou Daocheng in armor stood beneath the locust tree in the palace courtyard and, by the empress dowager's order, summoned Yuan Can, Chu Yuan, and Liu Bing to council.

sentences.zh: 道成謂秉曰：「此使君家事，何以斷之？」

translations.literal: Daocheng said to Bing: "This is your lordship's family affair—how do you judge it?"
translations.idiomatic: Daocheng said to Bing: "This is your family's affair—how do you judge it?"

sentences.zh: 秉未答。

translations.literal: Bing did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Bing did not answer.

sentences.zh: 道成鬚髯盡張，目光如電。

translations.literal: Daocheng's beard and whiskers bristled fully; his gaze was like lightning.
translations.idiomatic: Daocheng's beard bristled; his gaze flashed like lightning.

sentences.zh: 秉曰：「尚書眾事，可以見付；

translations.literal: Bing said: "The many affairs of the Masters of Writing may be entrusted to you;
translations.idiomatic: Bing said: "You may take charge of all civil affairs;

sentences.zh: 軍旅處分，一委領軍。」

translations.literal: disposition of military affairs—entrust them entirely to the Army Inspector."
translations.idiomatic: military affairs—leave them entirely to the army inspector."

sentences.zh: 道成次讓袁粲，粲亦不敢當。

translations.literal: Daocheng next yielded to Yuan Can; Can also dared not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Daocheng then deferred to Yuan Can, who also dared not accept.

sentences.zh: 王敬則拔白刃，在床側跳躍曰：「天下事皆應關蕭公！

translations.literal: Wang Jingze drew his bare blade, leaped beside the couch, and said: "All affairs under Heaven should concern Lord Xiao!
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jingze drew his naked blade, leaped beside the couch, and shouted: "All affairs under Heaven belong to Lord Xiao!

sentences.zh: 敢有開一言者，血染敬則刀！」

translations.literal: Whoever dares speak one word—let blood stain Jingze's blade!"
translations.idiomatic: Whoever dares object—let blood stain Jingze's blade!"

sentences.zh: 仍手取白紗帽加道成首，令即位，曰：「今日誰敢復動！

translations.literal: He then with his own hand took a white gauze cap and placed it on Daocheng's head, ordering him to take the throne, and said: "Who today would dare stir again!
translations.idiomatic: He then took a white gauze cap with his own hand, set it on Daocheng's head, and ordered him to take the throne, shouting: "Who would dare move against this today!

sentences.zh: 事須及熱！」

translations.literal: The affair must be seized while it is still hot!"
translations.idiomatic: Strike while the iron is hot!"

sentences.zh: 道成正色呵之曰：「卿都自不解！」

translations.literal: Daocheng sternly rebuked him, saying: "You simply do not understand at all!"
translations.idiomatic: Daocheng's face hardened as he shouted him down: "You don't understand a thing!"

sentences.zh: 粲欲有言，敬則叱之，乃止。

translations.literal: Can wished to speak; Jingze shouted him down, and he desisted.
translations.idiomatic: Can started to speak, but Jingze cut him off with a shout, and he fell silent.

sentences.zh: 褚淵曰：「非蕭公無以了此。」

translations.literal: Chu Yuan said: "Without Lord Xiao this cannot be brought to completion."
translations.idiomatic: Chu Yuan said: "Only Lord Xiao can see this through."

sentences.zh: 手取事授道成。

translations.literal: With his own hand he took the seal of office and handed it to Daocheng.
translations.idiomatic: He took the seal of office with his own hand and handed it to Daocheng.

sentences.zh: 道成曰：「相與不肯，我安得辭！」

translations.literal: Daocheng said: "You all refuse—how can I decline!"
translations.idiomatic: Daocheng said: "You all refuse the burden—how can I turn it down!"

sentences.zh: 乃下議，備法駕詣東城，迎立安成王。

translations.literal: He thereupon issued a decree; the full imperial escort was prepared and they went to the Eastern Palace to welcome and install the Prince of An.
translations.idiomatic: He then issued a decree, assembled the full imperial escort, and went to the Eastern Palace to welcome and install the Prince of An.

sentences.zh: 於是長刀遮粲、秉等，各失色而去。

translations.literal: Thereupon long blades barred Can, Bing, and the others; each paled and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Long blades then blocked Can, Bing, and the rest; each went pale and left.

sentences.zh: 秉出，於路逢從弟韞，韞開車迎問曰：「今日之事，當歸兄邪？」

translations.literal: When Bing left, on the road he met his younger clansman cousin Yun; Yun opened his carriage and greeted him, asking: "Today's affair—was it supposed to go to you, elder brother?"
translations.idiomatic: As Bing left, he met his younger cousin Yun on the road. Yun opened his carriage and called out: "Was today's prize meant for you, brother?"

sentences.zh: 秉曰：「吾等已讓領軍矣。」

translations.literal: Bing said: "We have already yielded to the Army Inspector."
translations.idiomatic: Bing said: "We already yielded to the army inspector."

sentences.zh: 韞拊膺曰：「兄肉中詎有血邪！

translations.literal: Yun beat his chest and said: "Brother, is there no blood in your flesh!
translations.idiomatic: Yun struck his chest and cried: "Brother, is there no blood in your veins!

sentences.zh: 今年族矣！」

translations.literal: This year the clan will be exterminated!"
translations.idiomatic: Our clan is finished this year!"

sentences.zh: 是日，以太后令，數蒼梧王罪惡，曰：「吾密令蕭領軍潛運明略。

translations.literal: That day, by the empress dowager's order, the crimes of the Deposed Emperor of Cangwu were enumerated, saying: "I secretly ordered the Army Inspector Xiao to deploy his wise strategy in secret.
translations.idiomatic: That day, by the empress dowager's order, the crimes of the deposed Emperor of Cangwu were listed, with the words: "I secretly ordered the army inspector Xiao to work out a wise plan in secret.

sentences.zh: 安成王准，宜臨萬國。」

translations.literal: Prince Zhun of An ought to ascend to rule the myriad states."
translations.idiomatic: Prince Zhun of An should take the throne and rule the realm."

sentences.zh: 追封昱為蒼梧王。

translations.literal: Yu was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Cangwu.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Cangwu.

sentences.zh: 儀衛至東府門，安成王令門者勿開，以待袁司徒。

translations.literal: When the ceremonial guard reached the eastern palace gate, the Prince of An ordered the gatekeepers not to open it, to await Minister Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: When the ceremonial escort reached the eastern palace gate, the Prince of An told the gatekeepers not to open it until Minister Yuan arrived.

sentences.zh: 粲至，王乃入居朝宮。

translations.literal: When Can arrived, the prince then entered and took residence in the audience palace.
translations.idiomatic: Once Can arrived, the prince entered and took up residence in the audience palace.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，王即皇帝位，時年十一。

translations.literal: On renchen the prince ascended the imperial throne; he was then eleven years old.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen the prince took the imperial throne. He was eleven years old.

sentences.zh: 改元，大赦。

translations.literal: The era name was changed and a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: The era name was changed and a general amnesty was declared.

sentences.zh: 葬蒼梧王於郊壇西。

translations.literal: The Deposed Emperor of Cangwu was buried west of the suburban altar.
translations.idiomatic: The deposed Emperor of Cangwu was buried west of the suburban altar.

sentences.zh: 魏京兆康王子推卒。

translations.literal: Prince Tui of Jingzhao Kang of Northern Wei died.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Tui of Jingzhao Kang of Northern Wei died.

sentences.zh: 甲午，蕭道成出鎮東府。

translations.literal: On jiawu Xiao Daocheng departed to garrison the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu Xiao Daocheng left to garrison the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 丙申，以道成為司空、錄尚書事、驃騎大將軍；

translations.literal: On bingshen Daocheng was made minister of works, recorder of masters of writing affairs, and grand general of agile cavalry;
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen Daocheng was appointed minister of works, recorder of masters of writing affairs, and grand general of agile cavalry;

sentences.zh: 袁粲遷中書監；

translations.literal: Yuan Can was transferred to supervisor of the Palace Secretariat;
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Can was transferred to supervisor of the Palace Secretariat;

sentences.zh: 褚淵加開府儀同三司；

translations.literal: Chu Yuan was granted the status of opening an office with protocol equal to the Three Excellencies;
translations.idiomatic: Chu Yuan was granted the status of opening an office with protocol equal to the Three Excellencies;

sentences.zh: 劉秉遷尚書令，加中領軍；

translations.literal: Liu Bing was transferred to master of writing and additionally made middle army inspector;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bing was made master of writing and additionally appointed middle army inspector;

sentences.zh: 以晉熙王燮為揚州刺史。

translations.literal: Prince Xie of Jinxi was made governor of Yang Province.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xie of Jinxi was appointed governor of Yang Province.

sentences.zh: 劉秉始謂尚書萬機，本以宗室居之，則天下無變；

translations.literal: Liu Bing had originally believed that if the myriad affairs of state handled by the masters of writing were held by the imperial clan, then there would be no upheaval in the realm;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bing had originally believed that if the imperial clan held the myriad affairs of the masters of writing, the realm would remain stable;

sentences.zh: 既而蕭道成兼總軍國，佈置心膂，與奪自專，褚淵素相憑附，秉與袁粲閣手仰成矣。

translations.literal: But then Xiao Daocheng took joint control of military and state affairs, placed his trusted men, and decided matters of promotion and demotion on his own authority; Chu Yuan had long relied on and attached himself to him, while Bing and Yuan Can sat with folded hands and looked upward as he accomplished it all.
translations.idiomatic: But then Xiao Daocheng took control of both military and civil affairs, installed his trusted men, and decided promotions and dismissals on his own. Chu Yuan had long attached himself to him, while Bing and Yuan Can stood aside with folded hands and let him have his way.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，以尚書右僕射王僧虔為僕射。

translations.literal: On xinchou Wang Sengqian, right vice-director of the masters of writing, was made vice-director of the masters of writing.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou Wang Sengqian, right vice-director of the masters of writing, was made vice-director of the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 丙午，以武陵王贊為郢州刺史；

translations.literal: On bingwu Prince Zan of Wuling was made governor of Ying Province;
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu Prince Zan of Wuling was appointed governor of Ying Province;

sentences.zh: 蕭道成改領南徐州刺史。

translations.literal: Xiao Daocheng was changed to additionally hold the governorship of South Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Daocheng was reassigned to hold the governorship of South Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 八月，壬子，魏大赦。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on renzi, Northern Wei proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on renzi, Northern Wei declared a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，詔袁粲鎮石頭。

translations.literal: On guihai an edict ordered Yuan Can to garrison Shitou.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai an edict ordered Yuan Can to garrison Shitou.

sentences.zh: 粲性沖靜，每有朝命，常固辭；

translations.literal: Can's nature was restrained and tranquil; whenever there was a court appointment, he regularly firmly declined;
translations.idiomatic: Can was by nature modest and retiring; whenever the court offered him an appointment, he usually refused firmly;

sentences.zh: 逼切不得已，乃就職。

translations.literal: when pressed urgently and with no alternative, he would then take the post.
translations.idiomatic: only when pressed hard and left no choice would he finally accept.

sentences.zh: 至是知蕭道成有不臣之志，陰欲圖之，即時受命。

translations.literal: On this occasion, knowing that Xiao Daocheng harbored disloyal ambitions, he secretly wished to plot against him and immediately accepted the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: This time, knowing Xiao Daocheng harbored disloyal ambitions, he secretly planned to move against him and accepted the post at once.

sentences.zh: 初，太宗使陳昭華母養順帝；

translations.literal: Previously, Emperor Taizong had Chen Zhaohua's mother rear Emperor Shun;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Emperor Taizong had Chen Zhaohua's mother raise Emperor Shun;

sentences.zh: 戊辰，尊昭華為皇太妃。

translations.literal: On wuchen Zhaohua was honored as imperial grand consort.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen Zhaohua was honored as imperial grand consort.

sentences.zh: 丙子，魏詔曰：「工商皁隸，各有厥分；

translations.literal: On bingzi Northern Wei issued an edict saying: "Artisans, merchants, clerks, and bondservants each have their allotted station;
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi Northern Wei issued an edict: "Artisans, merchants, clerks, and bondservants each have their proper place;

sentences.zh: 而有司縱濫，或染流俗。

translations.literal: yet the responsible officials indulge excess, and some are tainted by prevailing custom.
translations.idiomatic: yet officials have grown lax, and some have been corrupted by prevailing custom.

sentences.zh: 自今戶內有役者，唯止本部丞；

translations.literal: From now on, for households with corvée obligations, appointment shall stop at the clerk of the original department;
translations.idiomatic: From now on, for households subject to corvée, appointment shall go no higher than the clerk of the original department;

sentences.zh: 若有勳勞者，不從此制。」

translations.literal: those with merit and service are excepted from this rule."
translations.idiomatic: those with merit and service are exempt from this rule."

sentences.zh: 蕭道成固讓司空；

translations.literal: Xiao Daocheng firmly declined the post of minister of works;
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Daocheng firmly declined the post of minister of works;

sentences.zh: 庚辰，以為驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: On gengchen he was made grand general of agile cavalry with the status of opening an office equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen he was made grand general of agile cavalry with the status of opening an office equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 九月，乙酉，魏更定律令。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on yiyou, Northern Wei revised the laws and ordinances.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on yiyou, Northern Wei revised the laws and ordinances.

sentences.zh: 戊申，封楊玉夫等二十五人為侯、伯、子、男。

translations.literal: On wushen Yang Yufu and twenty-four others were enfeoffed as marquis, earl, viscount, and baron.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen Yang Yufu and twenty-four others were enfeoffed as marquis, earl, viscount, and baron.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，氐帥楊文度遣其弟文弘襲魏仇池，陷之。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, the Di chieftain Yang Wendu sent his younger brother Wenhong to raid Chou Chi of Northern Wei and captured it.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, the Di chieftain Yang Wendu sent his younger brother Wenhong to raid Northern Wei's Chou Chi and captured it.

sentences.zh: 初，魏徐州刺史李言斤，事顯祖為侖部尚書，信用盧奴令范檦。

translations.literal: Previously, Li Yanjin, governor of Xuzhou in Northern Wei, had served Emperor Xianwen as director of the Lun Department of the masters of writing and trusted Fan Biao, magistrate of Lu Nu.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, Li Yanjin, governor of Xuzhou in Northern Wei, had served Emperor Xianwen as director of the Lun Department of the masters of writing and placed his trust in Fan Biao, magistrate of Lu Nu.

sentences.zh: 言斤弟左將軍瑛諫曰：「檦能降人以色，假人以財，輕德義而重勢利；

translations.literal: Yanjin's younger brother, Left General Ying, remonstrated, saying: "Biao wins people over with appearance, lends people money, treats virtue and righteousness lightly and values power and profit heavily;
translations.idiomatic: Yanjin's younger brother, Left General Ying, remonstrated: "Biao wins people with charm and buys them with money. He treats virtue lightly and values power and profit;

sentences.zh: 聽其言也甘，察其行也賊，不早絕之，後悔無及。」

translations.literal: listening to his words is pleasant, but examining his conduct reveals treachery—if you do not cut him off early, you will regret it beyond remedy.
translations.idiomatic: his words are sweet, but his deeds are treacherous. If you do not cut him off now, you will regret it too late.

sentences.zh: 言斤不從，腹心之事，皆以語檦。

translations.literal: Yanjin did not listen; matters closest to his heart he told entirely to Biao.
translations.idiomatic: Yanjin would not listen and confided his innermost affairs entirely to Biao.

sentences.zh: 尚書越黑，與言斤皆有寵於顯祖，對掌選部。

translations.literal: Master of Writing Yue Hei and Yanjin were both favored by Emperor Xianwen and jointly managed the Selection Department.
translations.idiomatic: Master of writing Yue Hei and Yanjin were both favored by Emperor Xianwen and jointly managed the Selection Department.

sentences.zh: 言斤以其私用人為方州，黑對顯祖發之，由是有隙。

translations.literal: Yanjin used his private connections to appoint someone to a provincial governorship; Hei reported this to Emperor Xianwen, and from this there was a rift.
translations.idiomatic: Yanjin used his private connections to appoint someone to a provincial governorship. Hei reported it to Emperor Xianwen, and from that a rift opened between them.

sentences.zh: 頃之，言斤發黑前為監藏，盜用官物，黑坐黜為門士。

translations.literal: Before long, Yanjin exposed that Hei had previously served as treasury overseer and misused government goods; Hei was demoted to gate guard.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, Yanjin exposed Hei's earlier tenure as treasury overseer, when he had misused government goods. Hei was demoted to gate guard.

sentences.zh: 黑恨之，寢食為之衰少；

translations.literal: Hei hated him for this; his sleep and eating diminished on account of it;
translations.idiomatic: Hei hated him for it and ate and slept little;

sentences.zh: 逾年，復入為侍中、尚書左僕射，領選。

translations.literal: after more than a year, he reentered office as palace attendant, left vice-director of the masters of writing, and head of selection.
translations.idiomatic: after more than a year he returned as palace attendant, left vice-director of the masters of writing, and head of selection.

sentences.zh: 及顯祖殂，黑白馮太后，稱言斤專恣，出為徐州。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xianwen died, Hei spoke privately to Empress Dowager Feng, declaring that Yanjin acted arbitrarily, and Yanjin was sent out as governor of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xianwen died, Hei spoke privately to Empress Dowager Feng, saying Yanjin acted arbitrarily, and Yanjin was sent out as governor of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 范檦知太后怨言斤，乃告言斤謀外叛。

translations.literal: Fan Biao, knowing the empress dowager resented Yanjin, then reported that Yanjin plotted rebellion abroad.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Biao, knowing the empress dowager resented Yanjin, then reported that Yanjin was plotting to rebel abroad.

sentences.zh: 太后征言斤至平城問狀，言斤對無之，太后引檦使證之。

translations.literal: The empress dowager summoned Yanjin to Pingcheng to question him; Yanjin answered that there was no such thing; the empress dowager brought in Biao to bear witness.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager summoned Yanjin to Pingcheng to question him. Yanjin denied it, and the empress dowager brought in Biao to testify.

sentences.zh: 言斤謂檦曰：「汝今誣我，我復何言！

translations.literal: Yanjin said to Biao: "You now falsely accuse me—what more can I say!
translations.idiomatic: Yanjin said to Biao: "You falsely accuse me now—what more can I say!

sentences.zh: 然汝受我恩如此之厚，乃忍為爾乎！」

translations.literal: Yet the favor you received from me was so great—how can you bear to do this!"
translations.idiomatic: Yet the favor you received from me was so great—how can you bear to do this!"

sentences.zh: 檦曰：「檦受公恩，何如公受李敷恩！

translations.literal: Biao said: "The favor Biao received from Your Excellency—how does it compare with the favor Your Excellency received from Li Fu!
translations.idiomatic: Biao said: "The favor I received from Your Excellency—how does it compare with the favor Your Excellency received from Li Fu!

sentences.zh: 公忍之於敷，檦何為不忍於公！」

translations.literal: Your Excellency could be ruthless toward Fu—why should Biao not be ruthless toward Your Excellency!"
