translations.idiomatic: Your Excellency could be ruthless toward Fu—why should I not be ruthless toward you!"

sentences.zh: 言斤慨然歎曰：「吾不用瑛言，悔之何及！」

translations.literal: Yanjin sighed with emotion and said: "I did not heed Ying's words—regret comes too late!"
translations.idiomatic: Yanjin sighed and said: "I did not heed Ying's words—regret comes too late!"

sentences.zh: 趙黑復於中構成其罪，丙子，誅言斤及其子令和、令度；

translations.literal: Yue Hei again fabricated his crimes from within; on bingzi Yanjin and his sons Linghe and Lingdu were executed;
translations.idiomatic: Yue Hei again fabricated charges against him from within; on bingzi Yanjin and his sons Linghe and Lingdu were executed;

sentences.zh: 黑然後寢食如故。

translations.literal: Hei then slept and ate as before.
translations.idiomatic: Only then did Hei sleep and eat as before.

sentences.zh: 十一月，癸未，魏徵西將軍皮歡喜等三將軍帥眾四萬擊楊文弘。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on guiwei, Northern Wei's western campaign general Pi Huanxi and two other generals led forty thousand troops to attack Yang Wenhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on guiwei, Northern Wei's western campaign general Pi Huanxi and two other generals led forty thousand troops against Yang Wenhong.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，魏懷州民伊祁苟自稱堯後，聚眾於重山作亂；

translations.literal: On dinghai a commoner of Huai Province in Northern Wei, Yi Qigou, proclaimed himself a descendant of Yao and gathered a crowd at Mount Chong to rebel;
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai a commoner of Huai Province in Northern Wei, Yi Qigou, proclaimed himself a descendant of Yao and gathered a crowd at Mount Chong to rebel;

sentences.zh: 洛州刺史馮熙討滅之。

translations.literal: Feng Xi, governor of Luo Province, attacked and destroyed them.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Xi, governor of Luo Province, attacked and destroyed them.

sentences.zh: 馮太后欲盡誅闔城之民，雍州刺史張白澤諫曰：「凶渠逆黨，盡已梟夷；

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Feng wished to execute all the people within the city walls; Zhang Baize, governor of Yong Province, remonstrated, saying: "The ringleaders and rebellious faction have all been beheaded and killed;
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Feng wanted to execute everyone inside the city walls. Zhang Baize, governor of Yong Province, remonstrated: "The ringleaders and rebels have all been killed;

sentences.zh: 城中豈無忠良仁信之士，奈何不問白黑，一切誅之！」

translations.literal: surely among those within the city there are loyal, worthy, and trustworthy men—how can you without distinguishing guilt from innocence execute them all!
translations.idiomatic: surely the city holds loyal and trustworthy men—how can you kill them all without distinguishing the guilty from the innocent!

sentences.zh: 乃止。

translations.literal: She thereupon desisted.
translations.idiomatic: She desisted.

sentences.zh: 十二月，魏皮歡喜軍至建安，楊文弘棄城走。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Pi Huanxi's Northern Wei army reached Jian'an; Yang Wenhong abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Pi Huanxi's Northern Wei army reached Jian'an. Yang Wenhong abandoned the city and fled.

sentences.zh: 初，沈攸之與蕭道成於大明、景和之間同直殿省，深相親善，道成女為攸之子中書侍郎文和婦。

translations.literal: Previously, Shen Youzhi and Xiao Daocheng during the Daming and Jinghe eras had served together in the palace secretariat and were deeply friendly; Daocheng's daughter was the wife of Youzhi's son Wenhe, attendant-in-ordinary of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, Shen Youzhi and Xiao Daocheng had served together in the palace secretariat during the Daming and Jinghe eras and were close friends. Daocheng's daughter was married to Youzhi's son Wenhe, attendant-in-ordinary of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 攸之在荊州，直閣將軍高道慶，家在華容，假還，過江陵，與攸之爭戲槊。

translations.literal: When Youzhi was in Jing Province, the direct-palace general Gao Daoping, whose family was in Huarong, took leave and, passing through Jiangling, competed with Youzhi at spear-play.
translations.idiomatic: When Youzhi was in Jing Province, the direct-palace general Gao Daoping, whose family was in Huarong, took leave and, passing through Jiangling, competed with Youzhi at spear-play.

sentences.zh: 馳還建康。

translations.literal: He raced back to Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: He raced back to Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 言攸之反狀已成，請以三千人襲之。

translations.literal: He reported that Youzhi's signs of rebellion were already formed and requested three thousand men to strike him.
translations.idiomatic: He reported that Youzhi's rebellion was already taking shape and asked for three thousand men to strike him.

sentences.zh: 執政皆以為不可，道成仍保證其不然。

translations.literal: The chief ministers all deemed it impossible; Daocheng still guaranteed it was not so.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers all thought it impossible, and Daocheng still vouched that it was not so.

sentences.zh: 楊運長等惡攸之，密與道慶謀遣刺客殺攸之，不克。

translations.literal: Yang Yunchang and others hated Youzhi and secretly plotted with Daoping to send assassins to kill Youzhi; they did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yunchang and others hated Youzhi and secretly plotted with Daoping to send assassins against him, but failed.

sentences.zh: 會蒼梧王遇弒，主簿宗儼之、功曹臧寅勸攸之因此起兵。

translations.literal: When the Deposed Emperor of Cangwu met assassination, the registrar Zong Yanzhi and merit officer Zang Yin urged Youzhi to raise troops on this account.
translations.idiomatic: When the deposed Emperor of Cangwu was assassinated, the registrar Zong Yanzhi and merit officer Zang Yin urged Youzhi to raise troops on that pretext.

sentences.zh: 攸之以其長子元琰在建康為司徒左長史，故未發。

translations.literal: Youzhi, because his eldest son Yuanyan was in Jiankang serving as left chief clerk to the minister of education, did not yet act.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi did not act yet because his eldest son Yuanyan was in Jiankang serving as left chief clerk to the minister of education.

sentences.zh: 寅，凝之之子也。

translations.literal: Yin was the son of Ningzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Yin was the son of Ningzhi.

sentences.zh: 時楊運長等已不在內，蕭道成遣元琰以蒼梧王刳斫之具示攸之。

translations.literal: At this time Yang Yunchang and the others were no longer in the inner palace; Xiao Daocheng sent Yuanyan to show Youzhi the dissecting and chopping implements used on the Deposed Emperor of Cangwu.
translations.idiomatic: By then Yang Yunchang and the others were no longer in the inner palace. Xiao Daocheng sent Yuanyan to show Youzhi the dissecting and chopping tools used on the deposed Emperor of Cangwu.

sentences.zh: 攸之以道成名位素出己下，一旦專制朝權，心不平，謂元琰曰：「吾寧為王陵死，不為賈充生。」

translations.literal: Youzhi, because Daocheng's fame and rank had always been below his own yet now suddenly monopolized court power, was resentful and said to Yuanyan: "I would rather die like Wang Ling than live like Jia Chong."
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi resented that Daocheng, whose fame and rank had always been below his own, now suddenly monopolized court power. He said to Yuanyan: "I would rather die like Wang Ling than live like Jia Chong."

sentences.zh: 然亦未暇舉兵。

translations.literal: Yet he still had no leisure to raise troops.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he still had no time to raise troops.

sentences.zh: 乃上表稱慶，因留元琰。

translations.literal: He thereupon submitted a memorial offering congratulations and detained Yuanyan.
translations.idiomatic: He then submitted a memorial of congratulations and kept Yuanyan with him.

sentences.zh: 雍州刺史張敬兒，素與攸之司馬劉攘兵善，疑攸之將起事，密以問攘兵。

translations.literal: Zhang Jing'er, governor of Yong Province, was on good terms with Youzhi's chief administrator Liu Rangbing and suspected Youzhi was about to rise in rebellion; he secretly asked Rangbing about it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jing'er, governor of Yong Province, was on good terms with Youzhi's chief administrator Liu Rangbing and suspected Youzhi was about to rebel. He secretly asked Rangbing about it.

sentences.zh: 攘兵無所言，寄敬兒馬鐙一隻，敬兒乃為之備。

translations.literal: Rangbing said nothing but sent Jing'er one horse stirrup; Jing'er then made preparations.
translations.idiomatic: Rangbing said nothing but sent Jing'er a single horse stirrup. Jing'er then made preparations.

sentences.zh: 攸之有素書十數行，常韜在裲襠角，雲是明帝與己約誓。

translations.literal: Youzhi had a letter of more than ten lines in plain script, which he always kept hidden in the corner of his under-vest, saying it was a covenant sworn between him and Emperor Ming.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi had a letter of more than ten lines in plain script, which he always kept hidden in the corner of his under-vest, saying it was a covenant sworn between him and Emperor Ming.

sentences.zh: 攸之將舉兵，其妾崔氏諫曰：「官年已老，那不為百口計！」

translations.literal: When Youzhi was about to raise troops, his concubine Lady Cui remonstrated, saying: "My lord, you are already old—will you not consider your hundred mouths!"
translations.idiomatic: When Youzhi was about to raise troops, his concubine Lady Cui remonstrated: "My lord, you are already old—will you not think of your household!"

sentences.zh: 攸之指裲襠角示之，且稱太后使至，賜攸之燭，割之，得太后手令云：「社稷之事，一以委公。」

translations.literal: Youzhi pointed to the corner of his under-vest and showed it to her, and also claimed that an emissary from the empress dowager had arrived and presented Youzhi a candle; when it was cut open, inside was a handwritten order from the empress dowager saying: "Affairs of state—I entrust them entirely to you."
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi pointed to the corner of his under-vest and showed her, and also claimed an emissary from the empress dowager had arrived with a candle for him. When it was cut open, inside was a handwritten order from the empress dowager: "Affairs of state—I entrust them entirely to you."

sentences.zh: 於是勒兵移檄，遣使邀張敬兒及豫州刺史劉懷珍、梁州刺史梓潼范柏年、司州刺史姚道和、湘州行事庾佩玉、巴陵內史王文和同舉兵。

translations.literal: Thereupon he mustered troops and issued a proclamation, sending envoys to invite Zhang Jing'er, Liu Huaizhen governor of Yu Province, Fan Bonian of Zitong governor of Liang Province, Yao Daodao governor of Si Province, Yu Peiyu acting governor of Xiang Province, and Wang Wenhe interior administrator of Baling to rise together in arms.
translations.idiomatic: He then mustered troops and issued a proclamation, sending envoys to invite Zhang Jing'er, Liu Huaizhen governor of Yu Province, Fan Bonian of Zitong governor of Liang Province, Yao Daodao governor of Si Province, Yu Peiyu acting governor of Xiang Province, and Wang Wenhe interior administrator of Baling to rise in arms together.

sentences.zh: 敬兒、懷珍、文和並斬其使，馳表以聞；

translations.literal: Jing'er, Huaizhen, and Wenhe all executed the envoys and dispatched urgent reports to inform the throne;
translations.idiomatic: Jing'er, Huaizhen, and Wenhe all executed the envoys and sent urgent reports to the throne;

sentences.zh: 文和尋棄州奔夏口。

translations.literal: Wenhe soon abandoned his province and fled to Xiakou.
translations.idiomatic: Wenhe soon abandoned his province and fled to Xiakou.

sentences.zh: 柏年、道和、佩玉皆懷兩端。

translations.literal: Bonian, Daodao, and Peiyu all harbored divided loyalties.
translations.idiomatic: Bonian, Daodao, and Peiyu all sat on the fence.

sentences.zh: 道和，後秦高祖之孫也。

translations.literal: Daodao was a grandson of the Gaozu of Later Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Daodao was a grandson of the Gaozu of Later Qin.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，攸之遣輔國將軍孫同等相繼東下。

translations.literal: On xinyou, Youzhi sent Auxiliary State General Sun Tong and others to march east in succession.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou, Youzhi sent auxiliary state general Sun Tong and others to march east in succession.

sentences.zh: 攸之遺道成書，以為：「少帝昏狂，宜與諸公密議，共白太后，下令廢之；

translations.literal: Youzhi sent Daocheng a letter, writing: "The young emperor is muddleheaded and wild; you ought to confer in secret with the great ministers, jointly report to the empress dowager, and issue an order to depose him;
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi sent Daocheng a letter arguing: "The young emperor is muddleheaded and wild. You ought to confer in secret with the great ministers, report jointly to the empress dowager, and issue an order to depose him;

sentences.zh: 奈何交結左右，親行弒逆，乃至不殯，流蟲在戶？

translations.literal: Yet why do you cultivate the emperor's attendants, personally commit regicide, and go so far as to leave the corpse unburied with maggots streaming at the door?
translations.idiomatic: Yet why do you cultivate the emperor's attendants, commit regicide with your own hand, and go so far as to leave the corpse unburied with maggots streaming at the door?

sentences.zh: 凡在臣下，誰不惋駭！

translations.literal: Who among all subjects would not grieve and be appalled!
translations.idiomatic: Who among all subjects would not grieve and be appalled!

sentences.zh: 又，移易朝舊，佈置親黨，宮閣管籥，悉關家人。

translations.literal: Further, you have replaced long-standing court appointments, installed your own faction, and put the keys to palace gates entirely in the hands of kinsmen.
translations.idiomatic: Further, you have replaced long-standing court appointments, installed your own faction, and put the keys to palace gates entirely in the hands of kinsmen.

sentences.zh: 吾不知子孟、孔明遺訓固如此乎！

translations.literal: I did not know that the precepts left by Zimeng and Kongming were truly like this!
translations.idiomatic: I did not know the precepts left by Zimeng and Kongming were truly like this!

sentences.zh: 足下既有賊宋之心，吾寧敢捐包胥之節邪！」

translations.literal: Since you already harbor the intent to betray Song, how dare I cast aside the integrity of Shen Baoxu!"
translations.idiomatic: Since you already harbor the intent to betray Song, how dare I cast aside the integrity of Shen Baoxu!"

sentences.zh: 朝廷聞之，恟懼。

translations.literal: When the court heard this, it was alarmed and afraid.
translations.idiomatic: When the court heard this, it was alarmed and afraid.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，道成入守朝堂，命侍中蕭嶷代鎮東府，撫軍行參軍蕭映鎮京口。

translations.literal: On dingmao, Daocheng entered to guard the court hall; he ordered Palace Attendant Xiao Nie to replace him in guarding the Eastern Palace, and Pacification Army acting adjutant Xiao Ying to guard Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao, Daocheng entered to guard the court hall. He ordered palace attendant Xiao Nie to replace him at the Eastern Palace and pacification army acting adjutant Xiao Ying to hold Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 映，嶷之弟也。

translations.literal: Ying was Nie's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Ying was Nie's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，內外纂嚴。

translations.literal: On wuchen, martial law was proclaimed inside and outside.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen, martial law was proclaimed inside and outside.

sentences.zh: 己巳，以郢州刺史武陵王贊為荊州刺史。

translations.literal: On jisi, Prince Zan of Wuling, governor of Ying Province, was made governor of Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi, Prince Zan of Wuling, governor of Ying Province, was made governor of Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 庚午，以右衛將軍黃回為郢州刺史，督前鋒諸軍以討攸之。

translations.literal: On gengwu, Right Guard General Huang Hui was made governor of Ying Province and put in command of the vanguard forces to campaign against Youzhi.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu, right guard general Huang Hui was made governor of Ying Province and put in command of the vanguard forces to campaign against Youzhi.

sentences.zh: 初，道成以世子賾為晉熙王燮長史，行郢州事，修治器械以備攸之。

translations.literal: Initially, Daocheng had appointed his heir Ze as chief administrator to Prince Xie of Jinxi and acting governor of Ying Province, where he repaired weapons and equipment against Youzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Initially, Daocheng had appointed his heir Ze as chief administrator to Prince Xie of Jinxi and acting governor of Ying Province, where he repaired weapons and equipment against Youzhi.

sentences.zh: 及征燮為揚州，以賾為左衛將軍，與燮俱下。

translations.literal: When Xie was summoned to Yang Province, Ze was made Left Guard General and descended with Xie.
translations.idiomatic: When Xie was summoned to Yang Province, Ze was made left guard general and descended with Xie.

sentences.zh: 劉懷珍言於道成曰：「夏口衝要，宜得其人。」

translations.literal: Liu Huaizhen said to Daocheng: "Xiakou is a vital crossing—it needs the right man."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Huaizhen said to Daocheng: "Xiakou is a vital crossing—it needs the right man."

sentences.zh: 道成與賾書曰：「汝既入朝，當須文武兼資與汝意合者，委以後事。」

translations.literal: Daocheng wrote to Ze: "Since you are entering the capital, you must find someone with both civil and military talents who agrees with your thinking and entrust the aftermath to him."
translations.idiomatic: Daocheng wrote to Ze: "Since you are entering the capital, you must find someone with both civil and military talents who agrees with your thinking and entrust the aftermath to him."

sentences.zh: 賾乃薦燮司馬柳世隆自代。

translations.literal: Ze then recommended Xie's chief administrator Liu Shilong to succeed him.
translations.idiomatic: Ze then recommended Xie's chief administrator Liu Shilong to succeed him.

sentences.zh: 道成以世隆為武陵王贊長史，行郢州事。

translations.literal: Daocheng made Shilong chief administrator to Prince Zan of Wuling with authority over Ying Province affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Daocheng made Shilong chief administrator to Prince Zan of Wuling with authority over Ying Province affairs.

sentences.zh: 賾將行，謂世隆曰：「攸之一旦為變，焚夏口舟艦，沿流而東，不可制也。

translations.literal: As Ze was about to depart, he told Shilong: "If Youzhi suddenly mutinies, burns the ships at Xiakou, and sails downstream eastward, he cannot be checked.
translations.idiomatic: As Ze was about to depart, he told Shilong: "If Youzhi suddenly mutinies, burns the ships at Xiakou, and sails downstream eastward, he cannot be checked.

sentences.zh: 若得攸之留攻郢城，必未能猝拔。

translations.literal: If we can get Youzhi to linger and attack Ying city, he surely cannot take it in a rush.
translations.idiomatic: If we can get Youzhi to linger and attack Ying city, he surely cannot take it in a rush.

sentences.zh: 君為其內，我為其外，破之必矣。」

translations.literal: You hold the interior, I the exterior—we shall certainly defeat him."
translations.idiomatic: You hold the interior, I the exterior—we shall certainly defeat him."

sentences.zh: 及攸之起兵，賾行至尋陽，未得朝廷處分，眾欲倍道趨建康，賾曰：「尋陽地居中流，密邇畿甸。

translations.literal: When Youzhi raised troops, Ze reached Xunyang before receiving court orders; the troops wanted to race to Jiankang by forced marches. Ze said: "Xunyang lies in midstream, close to the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: When Youzhi raised troops, Ze reached Xunyang before receiving court orders. The troops wanted to race to Jiankang by forced marches. Ze said: "Xunyang lies in midstream, close to the capital region.

sentences.zh: 若留屯湓口，內籓朝廷，外援夏首，保據形勝，控制西南，今日會此，天所置也。」

translations.literal: If we hold Penkou, we can shield the court within and support Xiakou without—holding the strategic ground and controlling the southwest. To meet this place today is heaven's doing."
translations.idiomatic: If we hold Penkou, we can shield the court within and support Xiakou without—holding the strategic ground and controlling the southwest. To meet this place today is heaven's doing."

sentences.zh: 或以為湓口城小難固，左中郎將周山圖曰：「今據中流，為四方勢援，不可以小事難之；

translations.literal: Some thought Penkou's walls too small to defend firmly. Left Commandant Zhou Shantu said: "We now hold midstream as a pivot for all directions—it cannot be rejected over a trifle;
translations.idiomatic: Some thought Penkou's walls too small to defend firmly. Left commandant Zhou Shantu said: "We now hold midstream as a pivot for all directions—it cannot be rejected over a trifle;

sentences.zh: 苟眾心齊一，江山皆城隍也。」

translations.literal: If hearts are united, rivers and mountains themselves become walls and moats."
translations.idiomatic: If hearts are united, rivers and mountains themselves become walls and moats."

sentences.zh: 庚午，賾奉燮鎮湓口；

translations.literal: On gengwu, Ze escorted Xie to hold Penkou;
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu, Ze escorted Xie to hold Penkou;

sentences.zh: 賾悉以事委山圖。

translations.literal: Ze entrusted all affairs entirely to Shantu.
translations.idiomatic: Ze entrusted all affairs entirely to Shantu.

sentences.zh: 山圖斷取行旅船板以造樓櫓，立水柵，旬日皆辦。

translations.literal: Shantu requisitioned planks from passing vessels to build tower-ships, erected river barriers, and finished everything within ten days.
translations.idiomatic: Shantu requisitioned planks from passing vessels to build tower-ships, erected river barriers, and finished everything within ten days.

sentences.zh: 道成聞之，喜曰：「賾真我子也！」

translations.literal: Hearing of it, Daocheng rejoiced and said: "Ze is truly my son!"
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of it, Daocheng rejoiced and said: "Ze is truly my son!"

sentences.zh: 以賾為西討都督。

translations.literal: He appointed Ze commander for the western campaign.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Ze commander for the western campaign.

sentences.zh: 賾啟山圖為軍副。

translations.literal: Ze recommended Shantu as army deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Ze recommended Shantu as army deputy.

sentences.zh: 時江州刺史邵陵王友鎮尋陽，賾以為尋陽城不足固，表移友同鎮湓口，留江州別駕豫章胡諧之守尋陽。

translations.literal: At the time Prince You of Shaoling, governor of Jiang Province, held Xunyang. Ze thought Xunyang's walls insufficient for defense, memorialized to move You to hold Penkou jointly, and left Jiangzhou vice-governor Hu Xiezhi of Yuzhang to guard Xunyang.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Prince You of Shaoling, governor of Jiang Province, held Xunyang. Ze thought Xunyang's walls insufficient for defense, memorialized to move You to hold Penkou jointly, and left Jiangzhou vice-governor Hu Xiezhi of Yuzhang to guard Xunyang.

sentences.zh: 湘州刺史王蘊遭母喪罷歸，至巴陵，與沈攸之深相結。

translations.literal: Wang Yun, governor of Xiang Province, on finishing mourning for his mother and returning home, reached Baling and formed a deep bond with Shen Youzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yun, governor of Xiang Province, on finishing mourning for his mother and returning home, reached Baling and formed a deep bond with Shen Youzhi.

sentences.zh: 時攸之未舉兵，蘊過郢州，欲因蕭賾出吊作難，據郢城。

translations.literal: Youzhi had not yet raised troops. Yun passed through Ying Province, intending to take advantage of Xiao Ze coming out for mourning condolences to rebel and seize Ying city.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi had not yet raised troops. Yun passed through Ying Province, intending to take advantage of Xiao Ze coming out for mourning condolences to rebel and seize Ying city.

sentences.zh: 賾知之，不出。

translations.literal: Ze learned of it and did not come out.
translations.idiomatic: Ze learned of it and did not come out.

sentences.zh: 還，至東府，又欲因蕭道成出吊作難，道成又不出。

translations.literal: Returning to the Eastern Palace, he again intended to rebel when Xiao Daocheng came out for condolences; Daocheng also did not come out.
translations.idiomatic: Returning to the Eastern Palace, he again intended to rebel when Xiao Daocheng came out for condolences; Daocheng also did not come out.

sentences.zh: 蘊乃與袁粲、劉秉密謀誅道成，將帥黃回、任候伯、孫曇瓘、王宜興、卜伯興等皆與通謀。

translations.literal: Yun then plotted secretly with Yuan Can and Liu Bing to kill Daocheng; commanders Huang Hui, Ren Houbo, Sun Tanqiong, Wang Yixing, Bu Boxing, and others were all in on the conspiracy.
translations.idiomatic: Yun then plotted secretly with Yuan Can and Liu Bing to kill Daocheng; commanders Huang Hui, Ren Houbo, Sun Tanqiong, Wang Yixing, Bu Boxing, and others were all in on the conspiracy.

sentences.zh: 伯興，天與之子也。

translations.literal: Boxing was the son of Tianyu.
translations.idiomatic: Boxing was the son of Tianyu.

sentences.zh: 道成初聞攸之事起，自往詣粲，粲辭不見。

translations.literal: When Daocheng first heard that Youzhi's affair had erupted, he went personally to call on Can; Can declined and would not see him.
translations.idiomatic: When Daocheng first heard that Youzhi's affair had erupted, he went personally to call on Can; Can declined and would not see him.

sentences.zh: 通直郎袁達謂粲「不宜示異同」，粲曰：「彼若以主幼時艱，與桂陽時不異，劫我入台，我何辭以拒之！

translations.literal: Attendant Gentleman Yuan Da told Can "you ought not show disagreement." Can said: "If he, citing the difficulties of a young ruler no different from the Guiyang days, seizes me into the palace, what grounds would I have to refuse!
translations.idiomatic: Attendant gentleman Yuan Da told Can "you ought not show disagreement." Can said: "If he, citing the difficulties of a young ruler no different from the Guiyang days, seizes me into the palace, what grounds would I have to refuse!

sentences.zh: 一朝同止，欲異得乎！」

translations.literal: Once we lodge there together, how can we still differ!"
translations.idiomatic: Once we lodge there together, how can we still differ!"

sentences.zh: 道成乃召褚淵，與之連席，每事必引淵共之。

translations.literal: Daocheng then summoned Chu Yuan, sat with him at one mat, and on every matter consulted him jointly.
translations.idiomatic: Daocheng then summoned Chu Yuan, sat with him at one mat, and on every matter consulted him jointly.

sentences.zh: 時劉韞為領軍將軍，入直門下省；

translations.literal: At the time Liu Yun was Army Inspector, on duty at the Gate Attendants Department;
translations.idiomatic: At the time Liu Yun was army inspector, on duty at the Gate Attendants Department;

sentences.zh: 卜伯興為直閣，黃回等諸將皆出屯新亭。

translations.literal: Bu Boxing was duty commander at the pavilion gate; Huang Hui and the other generals all encamped at Xinting.
translations.idiomatic: Bu Boxing was duty commander at the pavilion gate; Huang Hui and the other generals all encamped at Xinting.

sentences.zh: 初，褚淵為衛將軍，遭母憂去職，朝廷敦迫，不起。

translations.literal: Initially, Chu Yuan was Guard General; on his mother's death he left office, but the court repeatedly pressed him and he would not resume.
translations.idiomatic: Initially, Chu Yuan was guard general; on his mother's death he left office, but the court repeatedly pressed him and he would not resume.

sentences.zh: 粲素有重名，自往譬說，淵乃從之。

translations.literal: Can, who had long enjoyed great reputation, went in person to persuade him, and Yuan then complied.
translations.idiomatic: Can, who had long enjoyed great reputation, went in person to persuade him, and Yuan then complied.

sentences.zh: 及粲為尚書令，遭母憂，淵譬說懇至，粲遂不起，淵由是恨之。

translations.literal: When Can became Director of the Masters of Writing and suffered his mother's death, Yuan pressed him earnestly to resume; Can still would not, and Yuan therefore resented him.
translations.idiomatic: When Can became director of the masters of writing and suffered his mother's death, Yuan pressed him earnestly to resume; Can still would not, and Yuan therefore resented him.

sentences.zh: 及沈攸之事起，道成與淵議之。

translations.literal: When Shen Youzhi's affair erupted, Daocheng discussed it with Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: When Shen Youzhi's affair erupted, Daocheng discussed it with Yuan.

sentences.zh: 淵曰：「西夏釁難，事必無成，公當先備其內耳。」

translations.literal: Yuan said: "The trouble rising in western Xia will surely fail; you should first secure matters within."
translations.idiomatic: Yuan said: "The trouble rising in western Xia will surely fail; you should first secure matters within."

sentences.zh: 粲謀既定，將以告淵；

translations.literal: The Can conspiracy was settled; they were about to tell Yuan;
translations.idiomatic: The Can conspiracy was settled; they were about to tell Yuan;

sentences.zh: 眾謂淵與道成素善，不可告。

translations.literal: The group said Yuan was on good terms with Daocheng and must not be told.
translations.idiomatic: The group said Yuan was on good terms with Daocheng and must not be told.

sentences.zh: 粲曰：「淵與彼雖善，豈容大作同異！

translations.literal: Can said: "Though Yuan is friendly with him, how could he permit a major break!
translations.idiomatic: Can said: "Though Yuan is friendly with him, how could he permit a major break!

sentences.zh: 今若不告，事定便應除之。」

translations.literal: If we do not tell him now, once the affair is settled he will surely be removed."
translations.idiomatic: If we do not tell him now, once the affair is settled he will surely be removed."

sentences.zh: 乃以謀告淵，淵即以告道成。

translations.literal: So they told Yuan the plot; Yuan immediately told Daocheng.
translations.idiomatic: So they told Yuan the plot; Yuan immediately told Daocheng.

sentences.zh: 道成亦先聞其謀，遣軍主蘇烈、薛淵、太原王天生將兵助粲守石頭。

translations.literal: Daocheng had also learned of the plot first; he sent army commanders Su Lie, Xue Yuan, and Wang Tiansheng of Taiyuan with troops to help Can hold Shitou.
translations.idiomatic: Daocheng had also learned of the plot first; he sent army commanders Su Lie, Xue Yuan, and Wang Tiansheng of Taiyuan with troops to help Can hold Shitou.

sentences.zh: 薛淵固辭，道成強之，淵不得已，涕泣拜辭，道成曰：「卿近在石頭，日夕去來，何悲如是，且又何辭？」

translations.literal: Xue Yuan firmly declined; Daocheng forced him. Yuan had no choice, weeping as he took leave. Daocheng said: "You will be close at Shitou, coming and going daily—why grieve so, and why take leave at all?"
translations.idiomatic: Xue Yuan firmly declined; Daocheng forced him. Yuan had no choice, weeping as he took leave. Daocheng said: "You will be close at Shitou, coming and going daily—why grieve so, and why take leave at all?"

sentences.zh: 淵曰：「不審公能保袁公共為一家否？

translations.literal: Yuan said: "I do not know whether you can ensure that Yuan Can and you remain one household?
translations.idiomatic: Yuan said: "I do not know whether you can ensure that Yuan Can and you remain one household?

sentences.zh: 今淵往，與之同則負公，不同則立受禍，何得不悲！」

translations.literal: If I go now, siding with him betrays you; not siding with him brings immediate disaster—how can I not grieve!"
translations.idiomatic: If I go now, siding with him betrays you; not siding with him brings immediate disaster—how can I not grieve!"

sentences.zh: 道成曰：「所以遣卿，正為能盡臨事之宜，使我無西顧之憂耳。

translations.literal: Daocheng said: "The reason I send you is precisely that you can handle affairs as they arise and leave me free of worry to the west.
translations.idiomatic: Daocheng said: "The reason I send you is precisely that you can handle affairs as they arise and leave me free of worry to the west.

sentences.zh: 但當努力，無所多言。」

translations.literal: Only exert yourself—say no more."
translations.idiomatic: Only exert yourself—say no more."

sentences.zh: 淵，安都之從子也。

translations.literal: Yuan was a nephew of Andu.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan was a nephew of Andu.

sentences.zh: 道成又以驍騎將軍王敬則為直閣，與伯興共總禁兵。

translations.literal: Daocheng also appointed Valiant Cavalry General Wang Jingze as duty commander at the pavilion, sharing command of the palace guard with Boxing.
translations.idiomatic: Daocheng also appointed valiant cavalry general Wang Jingze as duty commander at the pavilion, sharing command of the palace guard with Boxing.

sentences.zh: 粲謀矯太后令，使韞、伯興帥宿衛兵攻道成於朝堂，回等帥所領為應。

translations.literal: Can plotted to forge an empress dowager order sending Yun and Boxing to lead palace guards to attack Daocheng in the court hall, with Hui and the others leading their forces in support.
translations.idiomatic: Can plotted to forge an empress dowager order sending Yun and Boxing to lead palace guards to attack Daocheng in the court hall, with Hui and the others leading their forces in support.

sentences.zh: 劉秉、任候伯等並赴石頭，本期壬申夜發，秉恇擾不知所為，晡後即束裝；

translations.literal: Liu Bing, Ren Houbo, and the rest all went to Shitou. The plan was to act on the night of renshen; Bing, flustered and at a loss, began packing after midday;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bing, Ren Houbo, and the rest all went to Shitou. The plan was to act on the night of renshen; Bing, flustered and at a loss, began packing after midday;

sentences.zh: 臨去，啜羹，寫胸上，手振不自禁。

translations.literal: Before leaving he sipped soup; it spilled on his chest and his hands shook uncontrollably.
translations.idiomatic: Before leaving he sipped soup; it spilled on his chest and his hands shook uncontrollably.

sentences.zh: 未暗，載婦女，盡室奔石頭，部曲數百，赫奕滿道。

translations.literal: Before dark he loaded women and children—his whole household—and fled to Shitou, several hundred retainers thronging the road in grand array.
translations.idiomatic: Before dark he loaded women and children—his whole household—and fled to Shitou, several hundred retainers thronging the road in grand array.

sentences.zh: 既至，見粲，粲驚曰：「何事遽來？

translations.literal: When he arrived and saw Can, Can exclaimed: "Why have you come in such haste?
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived and saw Can, Can exclaimed: "Why have you come in such haste?

sentences.zh: 今敗矣！」

translations.literal: Now it is lost!"
translations.idiomatic: Now it is lost!"

sentences.zh: 秉曰：「得見公，萬死何恨！」

translations.literal: Bing said: "To see you, lord—even ten thousand deaths hold no regret!"
translations.idiomatic: Bing said: "To see you, lord—even ten thousand deaths hold no regret!"

sentences.zh: 孫曇瓘聞之，亦奔石頭。

translations.literal: Hearing of it, Sun Tanqiong also fled to Shitou.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of it, Sun Tanqiong also fled to Shitou.

sentences.zh: 丹陽丞王遜等走告道成，事乃大露。

translations.literal: Danyang assistant magistrate Wang Xun and others ran to inform Daocheng, and the affair was fully exposed.
translations.idiomatic: Danyang assistant magistrate Wang Xun and others ran to inform Daocheng, and the affair was fully exposed.

sentences.zh: 遜，僧綽之子也。

translations.literal: Xun was the son of Sengchuo.
translations.idiomatic: Xun was the son of Sengchuo.

sentences.zh: 道成密使人告王敬則。

translations.literal: Daocheng secretly sent word to Wang Jingze.
translations.idiomatic: Daocheng secretly sent word to Wang Jingze.

sentences.zh: 時閣已閉，敬則欲開閣出，卜伯興嚴兵為備，敬則乃鋸所止屋壁，得出，至中書省收韞。

translations.literal: The gate was already shut. Jingze wished to open the gate and go out; Bu Boxing had armed men on guard. Jingze sawed through the wall of his quarters to get out, went to the Secretariat to seize Yun.
translations.idiomatic: The gate was already shut. Jingze wished to open the gate and go out; Bu Boxing had armed men on guard. Jingze sawed through the wall of his quarters to get out, went to the Secretariat to seize Yun.

sentences.zh: 韞已成嚴，列燭自照。

translations.literal: Yun had already formed ranks and lined up candles to light himself.
translations.idiomatic: Yun had already formed ranks and lined up candles to light himself.

sentences.zh: 見敬則猝至，驚起迎之，曰：「兄何能夜顧？」

translations.literal: Seeing Jingze arrive suddenly, he started up in alarm to greet him and said: "Brother, how can you come calling at night?"
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Jingze arrive suddenly, he started up in alarm to greet him and said: "Brother, how can you come calling at night?"

sentences.zh: 敬則呵之曰：「小子那敢作賊！」

translations.literal: Jingze shouted at him: "You wretch—how dare you rebel!"
translations.idiomatic: Jingze shouted at him: "You wretch—how dare you rebel!"

sentences.zh: 韞抱敬則，敬則拳毆其頰仆地而殺之，又殺伯興。

translations.literal: Yun seized Jingze; Jingze punched him in the face, knocked him down, and killed him, and also killed Boxing.
translations.idiomatic: Yun seized Jingze; Jingze punched him in the face, knocked him down, and killed him, and also killed Boxing.

sentences.zh: 蘇烈等據倉城拒粲。

translations.literal: Su Lie and the others held Cangcheng to resist Can.
translations.idiomatic: Su Lie and the others held Cangcheng to resist Can.

sentences.zh: 王蘊聞秉已走，歎曰：「事不成矣！」

translations.literal: Wang Yun heard Bing had fled and sighed: "The affair is lost!"
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yun heard Bing had fled and sighed: "The affair is lost!"

sentences.zh: 狼狽帥部曲數百向石頭。

translations.literal: In disarray he led several hundred followers toward Shitou.
translations.idiomatic: In disarray he led several hundred followers toward Shitou.

sentences.zh: 本期開南門，時暗夜，薛淵據門射之。

translations.literal: The plan had been to open the south gate; it was dark night; Xue Yuan held the gate and shot at them.
translations.idiomatic: The plan had been to open the south gate; it was dark night; Xue Yuan held the gate and shot at them.

sentences.zh: 蘊謂粲已敗，即散走。

translations.literal: Yun thought Can had already been defeated and immediately scattered and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Yun thought Can had already been defeated and immediately scattered and fled.

sentences.zh: 道成遣軍主會稽戴僧靜帥數百人向石頭助烈等，自倉門得入，與之並力攻粲。

translations.literal: Daocheng sent army commander Dai Sengjing of Kuaiji with several hundred men toward Shitou to aid Lie and the others; they entered through Cang Gate and joined forces to attack Can.
translations.idiomatic: Daocheng sent army commander Dai Sengjing of Kuaiji with several hundred men toward Shitou to aid Lie and the others; they entered through Cang Gate and joined forces to attack Can.

sentences.zh: 孫曇瓘驍勇善戰，台軍死者百餘人。

translations.literal: Sun Tanqiong was fierce and skilled in battle; more than a hundred court troops died.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Tanqiong was fierce and skilled in battle; more than a hundred court troops died.

sentences.zh: 王天生殊死戰，故得相持，自亥至丑，戴僧靜分兵攻府西門，焚之，粲與秉在城東門，見火起，欲還赴府。

translations.literal: Wang Tiansheng fought desperately, so they could hold on—from hai to chou. Dai Sengjing divided his forces to attack the west gate of the headquarters, set it afire. Can and Bing were at the east gate; seeing the flames, they wished to return to the headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tiansheng fought desperately, so they could hold on—from hai to chou. Dai Sengjing divided his forces to attack the west gate of the headquarters, set it afire. Can and Bing were at the east gate; seeing the flames, they wished to return to the headquarters.

sentences.zh: 秉與二子俁、陔逾城走。

translations.literal: Bing with his two sons Yi and Gai climbed over the wall and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Bing with his two sons Yi and Gai climbed over the wall and fled.

sentences.zh: 粲下城，烈燭自照，謂其子最曰：「本知一木不能止大廈之崩，但以名義至此耳。」

translations.literal: Can came down from the wall, lit candles brightly, and said to his son Zui: "I always knew one timber cannot halt a great hall's collapse; I came this far only for honor's sake."
translations.idiomatic: Can came down from the wall, lit candles brightly, and said to his son Zui: "I always knew one timber cannot halt a great hall's collapse; I came this far only for honor's sake."

sentences.zh: 僧靜乘暗逾城獨進，最覺有異人，以身衛粲，僧靜直前斫之。

translations.literal: Sengjing, exploiting the darkness, climbed the wall and advanced alone. Zui sensed someone unusual and shielded Can with his body; Sengjing hacked forward and struck him.
translations.idiomatic: Sengjing, exploiting the darkness, climbed the wall and advanced alone. Zui sensed someone unusual and shielded Can with his body; Sengjing hacked forward and struck him.

sentences.zh: 粲謂最曰：「我不失忠臣，汝不失孝子！」

translations.literal: Can said to Zui: "I shall not fail as a loyal minister; you shall not fail as a filial son!"
translations.idiomatic: Can said to Zui: "I shall not fail as a loyal minister; you shall not fail as a filial son!"

sentences.zh: 遂父子俱死。

translations.literal: And so father and son both died.
translations.idiomatic: And so father and son both died.

sentences.zh: 百姓哀之，為之謠曰：「可憐石頭城，寧為袁粲死，不作褚淵生！」

translations.literal: The people mourned them and made a ballad: "Pitiable Shitou city—better die as Yuan Can than live as Chu Yuan!"
translations.idiomatic: The people mourned them and made a ballad: "Pitiable Shitou city—better die as Yuan Can than live as Chu Yuan!"

sentences.zh: 劉秉父子走至額簷湖，追執，斬之。

translations.literal: Liu Bing and his sons fled as far as Eyan Lake; pursued and captured, they were beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bing and his sons fled as far as Eyan Lake; pursued and captured, they were beheaded.

sentences.zh: 任候伯等並乘船赴石頭，既至，台軍已集，不得入，乃馳還。

translations.literal: Ren Houbo and the others all took boats toward Shitou; when they arrived, court troops had already gathered and they could not enter, so they galloped back.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Houbo and the others all took boats toward Shitou; when they arrived, court troops had already gathered and they could not enter, so they galloped back.

sentences.zh: 黃回嚴兵，期詰旦帥所領從御道直向台門攻道成。

translations.literal: Huang Hui drew up his troops in battle order, planning at dawn to lead his command straight along the imperial way to the palace gate to attack Daocheng.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Hui drew up his troops in battle order, planning at dawn to lead his command straight along the imperial way to the palace gate to attack Daocheng.

sentences.zh: 聞事洩，不敢發。

translations.literal: Hearing the plot had leaked, he dared not act.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing the plot had leaked, he dared not act.

sentences.zh: 道成撫之如舊。

translations.literal: Daocheng treated him as before.
translations.idiomatic: Daocheng treated him as before.

sentences.zh: 王蘊、孫曇瓘皆逃竄，先捕得蘊，斬之，其餘粲黨皆無所問。

translations.literal: Wang Yun and Sun Tanqiong both fled; Yun was captured first and beheaded; the rest of Can's faction were not pursued.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yun and Sun Tanqiong both fled; Yun was captured first and beheaded; the rest of Can's faction were not pursued.

sentences.zh: 粲典簽莫嗣祖為粲、秉宣通密謀，道成召詰之曰：「袁粲謀反，何不啟聞？」

translations.literal: Can's chief clerk Mo Sizu had transmitted the secret plot for Can and Bing. Daocheng summoned and interrogated him: "Yuan Can plotted rebellion—why did you not report it?"
translations.idiomatic: Can's chief clerk Mo Sizu had transmitted the secret plot for Can and Bing. Daocheng summoned and interrogated him: "Yuan Can plotted rebellion—why did you not report it?"

sentences.zh: 嗣祖曰：「小人無識，但知報恩，何敢洩其大事！

translations.literal: Sizu said: "This petty man is without understanding; I only know to repay kindness—how would I dare leak their great affair!
translations.idiomatic: Sizu replied: "I am a man of no discernment. I knew only to repay a debt of kindness—how could I betray so weighty a plot?

sentences.zh: 今袁公已死，義不求生。」

translations.literal: Now Lord Yuan is already dead; by righteousness I do not seek to live."
translations.idiomatic: Lord Yuan is dead. Righteousness allows me no wish to live on."

sentences.zh: 蘊嬖人張承伯藏匿蘊，道成並赦而用之。

translations.literal: Yun's favorite Zhang Chengbo had hidden Yun; Daocheng pardoned both and put them to use.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chengbo, a retainer favored by Yun, had concealed Yun. Daocheng pardoned them both and kept them in service.

sentences.zh: 粲簡淡平素，而無經世之才；

translations.literal: Can was simple, dispassionate, and unassuming by nature, yet lacked the talent to order the age;
translations.idiomatic: Can lived simply and temperately by habit, but he lacked the talent to govern an age in crisis;

sentences.zh: 好飲酒，喜吟諷，身居劇任，不肯當事；

translations.literal: he loved drinking wine and delighted in chanting verses; though holding a weighty post, he refused to manage affairs;
translations.idiomatic: He loved wine and delighted in reciting poetry; though he held heavy responsibility, he would not attend to business.

sentences.zh: 主事每往咨決，或高詠對之。

translations.literal: when those in charge of affairs came to consult and decide, he would sometimes reply with lofty song.
translations.idiomatic: When administrators came for counsel, he would sometimes answer with sung verse.

sentences.zh: 閒居高臥，門無雜賓，物情不接，故及於敗。

translations.literal: at leisure he lay high and long at home; his gate had no mixed guests; worldly affairs did not reach him—hence he came to ruin.
translations.idiomatic: In idle hours he reclined at home; no casual guests crossed his threshold, and public affairs never touched him—thus he met defeat.

sentences.zh: 裴子野論曰：袁景倩，民望國華，受付託之重；

translations.literal: Pei Ziye commented: Yuan Jingqian had the people's hope and the state's glory; he received the weight of entrustment;
translations.idiomatic: Pei Ziye wrote: Yuan Jingqian commanded the people's esteem and the state's regard, and bore a grave charge of trust;

sentences.zh: 智不足以除奸，權不足以處變，蕭條散落，危而不扶。

translations.literal: his wisdom was insufficient to remove traitors, his authority insufficient to meet change; [all] withered and scattered—in peril yet unshored up.
translations.idiomatic: His wisdom could not root out treachery, nor his authority master sudden change. All dwindled and scattered; peril came, and he did not brace what was falling.

sentences.zh: 及九鼎既輕，三才將換，區區斗城之裡，出萬死而不辭，蓋蹈匹夫之節，而無棟樑之具矣！

translations.literal: When the nine cauldrons had already grown light and heaven, earth, and man were about to change, within the mere compass of Dou City he went forth without flinching at ten thousand deaths—surely he fulfilled a common man's integrity, yet lacked what makes a pillar and beam!
translations.idiomatic: When the throne itself had grown hollow and the order of heaven, earth, and man stood ready to turn, within the cramped walls of Dou City he faced death without flinching—proof of an ordinary man's honor, but not the making of a statesman who could bear the realm's weight.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，大赦。

translations.literal: On jiaxu a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu a general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，以尚書僕射王僧虔為左僕射，新除中書令王延之為右僕射，度支尚書張岱為吏部尚書，吏部尚書王奐為丹陽尹。

translations.literal: On yihai Wang Sengqian, vice director of the masters of writing, was made left vice director; the newly appointed director of the secretariat Wang Yanzhi was made right vice director; Zhang Dai, minister of revenue, was made minister in charge of the officials; and Wang Huan, minister in charge of the officials, was made governor of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai Wang Sengqian, vice director of the masters of writing, was appointed left vice director; Wang Yanzhi, newly made director of the secretariat, was made right vice director; Zhang Dai, minister of revenue, became minister in charge of the officials; and Wang Huan, minister in charge of the officials, became governor of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 延之，裕之孫也。

translations.literal: Yanzhi was the grandson of Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhi was the grandson of Yu.

sentences.zh: 劉秉弟遐為吳郡太守。

translations.literal: Liu Bing's younger brother Xia was governor of Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bing's younger brother Xia served as governor of Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 司徒右長史張瑰，永之子也，遭父喪在吳，家素豪盛，蕭道成使瑰伺間取遐。

translations.literal: Zhang Gui, right chief clerk to the minister of works, was Yong's son; mourning his father in Wu, his household had long been wealthy and powerful, and Xiao Daocheng had Gui watch for an opening to seize Xia.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Gui, right chief clerk to the minister of works and a son of Yong, was mourning his father in Wu. His family had long been rich and powerful, and Xiao Daocheng ordered Gui to seize Xia when the moment came.

sentences.zh: 會遐召瑰詣府，瑰帥部曲十餘人直入齋中，執遐，斬之，郡中莫敢動。

translations.literal: When Xia summoned Gui to the headquarters, Gui led more than ten retainers straight into the study, seized Xia, beheaded him, and no one in the commandery dared stir.
translations.idiomatic: When Xia summoned Gui to his headquarters, Gui led a dozen retainers straight into the study, seized Xia, and beheaded him. No one in the commandery dared move.

sentences.zh: 道成聞之，以告瑰從父領軍沖，沖曰：「瑰以百口一擲，出手得盧矣。」

translations.literal: Daocheng heard of it and told Gui's uncle by marriage, the camp commander Chong; Chong said: "Gui staked a hundred lives on one throw and came up with the highest cast at once."
translations.idiomatic: Daocheng reported it to Gui's uncle by marriage, camp commander Chong, who said: "Gui wagered a hundred lives on one throw—and rolled the winning face at once."

sentences.zh: 道成即以瑰為吳郡太守。

translations.literal: Daocheng thereupon made Gui governor of Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Daocheng thereupon appointed Gui governor of Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 道成移屯閱武堂，猶以重兵付黃回使西上，而配以腹心。

translations.literal: Daocheng moved his camp to the Review Martial Hall; he still entrusted heavy forces to Huang Hui for a westward advance, pairing him with trusted intimates.
translations.idiomatic: Daocheng shifted his headquarters to the Review Martial Hall. He still sent Huang Hui west with a strong force, but paired him with men he trusted completely.

sentences.zh: 回素與王宜興不協，恐宜興反告其謀，閏月，辛巳，因事收宜興，斬之。

translations.literal: Hui had long been at odds with Wang Yixing and feared Yixing would turn and expose his plot; in the intercalary month, on xinsi, he seized Yixing on a pretext and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Hui had long been at odds with Wang Yixing and feared Yixing would denounce his plot. In the intercalary month, on xinsi, he seized Yixing on a pretext and beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 諸將皆言回握強兵必反，寧朔將軍桓康請獨往刺之，道成曰：「卿等何疑！

translations.literal: The generals all said that with strong troops in his grip Hui was sure to rebel; the general who calms the north, Huan Kang, asked to go alone and assassinate him. Daocheng said: "Why do you doubt him!
translations.idiomatic: The generals all warned that Hui, holding a powerful army, would surely rebel. General who calms the north Huan Kang offered to go alone and kill him. Daocheng said: "Why do you doubt him!

sentences.zh: 彼無能為也。」

translations.literal: He can do nothing."
translations.idiomatic: He can do nothing."

sentences.zh: 沈攸之遣中兵參軍孫同等五將以三萬人為前驅，司馬劉攘兵等五將以二萬人次之；

translations.literal: Shen Youzhi sent the middle army adjutant Sun Tong and five other generals with thirty thousand men as the vanguard, and the marshal Liu Rangbing and five other generals with twenty thousand as the second echelon;
translations.idiomatic: Shen Youzhi sent middle army adjutant Sun Tong and five other generals ahead with thirty thousand men, and marshal Liu Rangbing and five other generals with twenty thousand in the second wave;

sentences.zh: 又遣中兵參軍王靈秀等四將分兵出夏口，據魯山。

translations.literal: he also sent the middle army adjutants Wang Lingxiu and three other generals to divide their forces out of Xiakou and hold Lushan.
translations.idiomatic: he also sent middle army adjutants Wang Lingxiu and three other generals to split off from Xiakou and seize Lushan.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，攸之至夏口，自恃兵強，有驕色。

translations.literal: On guisi Youzhi reached Xiakou; trusting in his army's strength, he wore a proud look.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi Youzhi reached Xiakou. Confident in his army's strength, he wore a proud air.

sentences.zh: 以郢城弱小，不足攻，云「欲問訊安西」，暫泊黃金浦，遣人告柳世隆曰：「被太后令，當暫還都。

translations.literal: He thought Ying city small and weak, not worth attacking, saying he "wished to call on the governor of the west" and temporarily anchored at Golden Harbor, sending word to Liu Shilong: "By the empress dowager's order I am to return briefly to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He judged Ying city too small and weak to bother with, saying he wished only "to pay a visit west of the capital." He anchored briefly at Golden Harbor and sent word to Liu Shilong: "By the empress dowager's order I am to return briefly to the capital.

sentences.zh: 卿既相與奉國，想得此意。」

translations.literal: You and I alike serve the state—I trust you grasp my meaning.
translations.idiomatic: You and I alike serve the state. I trust you understand my intent.

sentences.zh: 世隆曰：「東下之師，久承聲問。

translations.literal: Shilong said: "The army coming east has long been awaited.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong replied: "Your army coming east has long been expected.

sentences.zh: 郢城小鎮，自守而已。」

translations.literal: Ying is a small town—it can only hold itself.
translations.idiomatic: Ying is a small fortress. It can only defend itself."

sentences.zh: 宗儼之勸攸之攻郢城；

translations.literal: Zong Yanzhi urged Youzhi to attack Ying city;
translations.idiomatic: Zong Yanzhi urged Youzhi to attack Ying city;

sentences.zh: 臧寅以為：「郢城兵雖少而地險，攻守勢異，非旬日可拔。

translations.literal: Zang Yin argued: "Though Ying has few troops, the ground is perilous; offense and defense differ in advantage, and it cannot be taken in ten days.
translations.idiomatic: Zang Yin argued: "Ying has few troops, but the terrain is dangerous. Attack and defense are not the same contest, and the city cannot be taken in ten days.

sentences.zh: 若不時舉，挫銳損威，今順流長驅，計日可捷。

translations.literal: If we fail to strike in time, we will blunt our edge and lose prestige. Now, driving downstream at full speed, victory can be counted by days.
translations.idiomatic: If we linger, we blunt our edge and lose prestige. Drive downstream at speed, and victory can be counted in days.

sentences.zh: 既傾根本，則郢城豈能自固！」

translations.literal: Once the root is overturned, how can Ying hold itself!
translations.idiomatic: Once the root is overturned, how can Ying hold out on its own?"

sentences.zh: 攸之從其計，欲留偏師守郢城，自將大眾東下。

translations.literal: Youzhi followed this plan, intending to leave a detached force to hold Ying while he himself led the main host east.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi took this advice and planned to leave a detachment at Ying while he led the main force east.

sentences.zh: 乙未，將發，柳世隆遣人於西渚挑戰，前軍中兵參軍焦度於城樓上肆言罵攸之，且穢辱之。

translations.literal: On yiwei, as he was about to depart, Liu Shilong sent men to challenge him at the western ford; the vanguard's middle army adjutant Jiao Du on the tower railed at Youzhi and reviled him with filth.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei, as he prepared to depart, Liu Shilong sent men to challenge him at the western ford. From the tower, vanguard middle army adjutant Jiao Du cursed Youzhi and heaped filth on his name.

sentences.zh: 攸之怒，改計攻城，令諸軍登岸燒郭邑，築長圍，晝夜攻戰。

translations.literal: Youzhi grew angry, changed his plan, and ordered an assault on the city; he had the armies go ashore, burn the outer settlements, build a long encirclement, and attack day and night.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Youzhi changed plans and ordered an assault. His armies went ashore, burned the outer settlements, built a long encirclement, and attacked day and night.

sentences.zh: 世董隨宜拒應，攸之不能克。

translations.literal: Shilong met each move as suited the moment; Youzhi could not overcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong met each move as the moment required, and Youzhi could not take the city.

sentences.zh: 道成命吳興太守沈文秀督吳、錢唐軍事。

translations.literal: Daocheng ordered Shen Wenxiu, governor of Wuxing, to oversee military affairs in Wu and Qiantang.
translations.idiomatic: Daocheng ordered Wuxing governor Shen Wenxiu to oversee military affairs in Wu and Qiantang.

sentences.zh: 文秀收攸之弟新安太守登之，誅其宗族。

translations.literal: Wenxiu seized Youzhi's younger brother Dengzhi, governor of Xin'an, and executed his clan.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiu seized Youzhi's younger brother Dengzhi, governor of Xin'an, and put his entire clan to death.

sentences.zh: 乙未，以後軍將軍楊運長為宣城太守；

translations.literal: On yiwei the rear army general Yang Yunchang was made governor of Xuancheng;
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei rear army general Yang Yunchang was appointed governor of Xuancheng;

sentences.zh: 於是太宗嬖臣無在禁省者矣。

translations.literal: thus none of the late emperor's favorite retainers remained in the inner palace offices.
translations.idiomatic: and so none of the late emperor's favorite retainers remained in the inner palace offices.

sentences.zh: 沈約論曰：「夫人君南面，九重奧絕，陪奉朝夕，義隔卿士，階闥之任，宜有司存。

translations.literal: Shen Yue commented: "When the ruler faces south, the ninefold inner palace is deep and sealed; those who attend morning and evening stand apart from ministers and grandees by ritual, and gate-and-door duties ought to belong to proper offices.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Yue wrote: "When the ruler faces south, the inner palace stands nine gates deep and sealed off. Those who attend him morning and evening are set apart from ministers and grandees by ritual, and duties at the threshold ought to belong to proper offices.

sentences.zh: 既而恩以狎生，信由恩固，無可憚之姿，有易親之色。

translations.literal: Yet intimacy breeds favor, and trust is fixed by favor; there is no posture to fear, and an air easy to draw near.
translations.idiomatic: Yet intimacy breeds favor, and trust grows from favor. Such men have nothing to fear and an air that invites closeness.

sentences.zh: 孝建、泰始，主威獨運，而刑政糾雜，理難遍通，耳目所寄，事歸近習。

translations.literal: In the Xiaojian and Taishi eras the sovereign's authority stood alone, while punishments and governance were tangled and hard to reach everywhere; what the eyes and ears relied on fell to near attendants.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xiaojian and Taishi eras the sovereign's authority stood alone, while punishments and governance were tangled and hard to reach everywhere. What the eyes and ears relied on fell to near attendants.

sentences.zh: 及覘歡慍，候慘舒，動中主情，舉無謬旨；

translations.literal: When they watched for joy or anger, waited on gloom or ease, and moved within the ruler's feelings, nothing they undertook missed the mark;
translations.idiomatic: They watched for joy or anger, waited on gloom or ease, and moved within the ruler's feelings—nothing they undertook missed the mark;

sentences.zh: 人主謂其身卑位薄，以為權不得重。

translations.literal: the ruler thought their persons lowly and their posts slight, and believed power could not weigh heavily in their hands.
translations.idiomatic: the ruler thought their persons lowly and their posts slight, and believed power could not weigh heavily in their hands.

sentences.zh: 曾不知鼠憑社貴，狐藉虎威，外無逼主之嫌，內有專用之效，勢傾天下，未之或悟。

translations.literal: He did not know that a rat relying on its mound is held precious, and a fox borrowing a tiger's might—without outward suspicion of forcing the ruler, yet with inward effect of sole use—can tilt the realm, and none awaken to it.
translations.idiomatic: He did not see that a rat relying on its mound is held precious, and a fox borrowing a tiger's might—without outward suspicion of forcing the ruler, yet with inward effect of sole use—can tilt the whole realm, and none awaken to it.

sentences.zh: 及太宗晚運，慮經盛衰，權幸之徒，懾憚宗戚，欲使幼主孤立，永竊國權，構造同異，興樹禍隙，帝弟宗王，相繼屠剿，寶祚夙傾，實由於此矣。

translations.literal: When the late emperor's final years brought fear of rise and fall, those who held favor dreaded the imperial clan; wishing to isolate the young ruler and hold power forever, they stirred division and planted the seeds of disaster. The emperor's younger brothers and princes of the blood were slaughtered one after another; the throne was overthrown early—truly this was the cause.
translations.idiomatic: When the late emperor's final years brought fear of rise and fall, those who held favor dreaded the imperial clan. Wishing to isolate the young ruler and hold power forever, they stirred division and planted the seeds of disaster. The emperor's younger brothers and princes of the blood were slaughtered one after another; the throne was overthrown early—and truly this was the cause.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，尚書左丞濟陽江謐建議假蕭道成黃鉞，從之。

translations.literal: On xinchou Jiang Mi of Jiyang, left assistant director of the masters of writing, proposed lending Xiao Daocheng the yellow battle-axe; the court approved.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou Jiang Mi of Jiyang, left assistant director of the masters of writing, proposed lending Xiao Daocheng the yellow battle-axe; the court approved.

sentences.zh: 加北秦州刺史武都王楊文度都督北秦、雍二州諸軍事，以龍驤將軍楊文弘為略陽太守。

translations.literal: Prince Wudu Yang Wendu, governor of northern Qin, was made area commander over the armies of northern Qin and Yong; the dragon-courage general Yang Wenhong was made governor of Lueyang.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Wudu Yang Wendu, governor of northern Qin, was made area commander over the armies of northern Qin and Yong; dragon-courage general Yang Wenhong was made governor of Lueyang.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，魏皮歡喜拔葭蘆，斬文度。

translations.literal: On renyin the Wei general Pi Huanxi took Jialu and beheaded Wendu.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin the Wei general Pi Huanxi took Jialu and beheaded Wendu.

sentences.zh: 魏以楊難當族弟廣香為陰平公、葭蘆戍主，用詔歡喜築駱谷城。

translations.literal: The Wei made Yang Nandang's clansman Guangxiang duke of Yinping and garrison commander at Jialu, and ordered Huanxi to build Luogu city.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei made Yang Nandang's clansman Guangxiang duke of Yinping and garrison commander at Jialu, and ordered Huanxi to build Luogu city.

sentences.zh: 文弘奉表謝罪於魏，遣子苟奴入侍。

translations.literal: Wenhong submitted a memorial to the Wei accepting blame and sent his son Gounu to serve at court.
translations.idiomatic: Wenhong submitted a memorial to the Wei accepting blame and sent his son Gounu to serve at court.

sentences.zh: 魏以文弘為南秦州刺史、武都王。

translations.literal: The Wei made Wenhong governor of southern Qin and prince of Wudu.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei made Wenhong governor of southern Qin and prince of Wudu.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，蕭道成出頓新亭，謂驃騎參軍江淹曰：「天下紛紛，君謂何如？」

translations.literal: On yisi Xiao Daocheng went out and encamped at Xinting; he said to the swift-cavalry adjutant Jiang Yan: "The realm is in turmoil—what do you think?
translations.idiomatic: On yisi Xiao Daocheng went out and encamped at Xinting. He asked swift-cavalry adjutant Jiang Yan: "The realm is in turmoil—what do you think?

sentences.zh: 淹曰：「成敗在德，不在眾寡。

translations.literal: Yan said: "Victory and defeat lie in virtue, not in numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Yan said: "Victory and defeat lie in virtue, not in numbers.

sentences.zh: 公雄武有奇略，一勝也；

translations.literal: My lord is bold in war and rich in stratagem—that is one victory;
translations.idiomatic: My lord is bold in war and rich in stratagem—that is one victory;

sentences.zh: 寬容而仁恕，二勝也；

translations.literal: broad-minded and merciful—that is two;
translations.idiomatic: broad-minded and merciful—that is two;

sentences.zh: 賢能畢力，三勝也；

translations.literal: the worthy and able give all their strength—that is three;
translations.idiomatic: the worthy and able give all their strength—that is three;

sentences.zh: 民望所歸，四勝也；

translations.literal: the people's hope gathers to you—that is four;
translations.idiomatic: the people's hope gathers to you—that is four;

sentences.zh: 奉天子以伐叛逆，五勝也。

translations.literal: upholding the Son of Heaven to punish rebellion—that is five.
translations.idiomatic: upholding the Son of Heaven to punish rebellion—that is five.

sentences.zh: 彼志銳而器小，一敗也；

translations.literal: Their will is sharp but their capacity small—that is one defeat;
translations.idiomatic: Their will is sharp but their capacity small—that is one defeat;

sentences.zh: 有威而無恩，二敗也；

translations.literal: they have awe but no kindness—that is two;
translations.idiomatic: they have awe but no kindness—that is two;

sentences.zh: 士卒解體，三敗也；

translations.literal: the soldiers are coming apart—that is three;
translations.idiomatic: the soldiers are coming apart—that is three;

sentences.zh: 搢紳不懷，四敗也；

translations.literal: the gentry do not incline to them—that is four;
translations.idiomatic: the gentry do not incline to them—that is four;

sentences.zh: 懸兵數千里，而無同惡相濟，五敗也。

translations.literal: they hang their army a thousand li away with no ally of shared hatred to help—that is five.
translations.idiomatic: they hang their army a thousand li away with no ally of shared hatred to help—that is five.

sentences.zh: 雖豺狼十萬，終為我獲。」

translations.literal: Though they be wolves by the hundred thousand, in the end they will be ours to take.
translations.idiomatic: Though they be wolves by the hundred thousand, in the end they will be ours to take."

sentences.zh: 道成笑曰：「君談過矣！」

translations.literal: Daocheng smiled and said: "You talk too much!
translations.idiomatic: Daocheng smiled and said: "You talk too much!"

sentences.zh: 南徐州行事劉善明言於道成曰：「攸之收眾聚騎，造舟治械，苞藏禍心，於今十年。

translations.literal: Liu Shanming, acting governor of southern Xu, said to Daocheng: "Youzhi has gathered troops and horses, built boats and readied weapons, and nursed treacherous intent for ten years now.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shanming, acting governor of southern Xu, said to Daocheng: "Youzhi has gathered troops and horses, built boats and readied weapons, and nursed treacherous intent for ten years now.

sentences.zh: 性既險躁，才非持重；

translations.literal: His nature is treacherous and rash, and his talent is not steady;
translations.idiomatic: His nature is treacherous and rash, and his talent is not steady;

sentences.zh: 而起逆累旬，遲回不進。

translations.literal: yet having raised rebellion for many days, he hesitates and does not advance.
translations.idiomatic: yet having raised rebellion for many days, he hesitates and does not advance.

sentences.zh: 一則暗於兵機，二則人情離怨，三則有掣肘之患，四則天奪其魄。

translations.literal: First, he is blind to the chances of war; second, hearts are estranged and resentful; third, he suffers the trouble of being held back; fourth, heaven has taken his wits.
translations.idiomatic: First, he is blind to the chances of war; second, hearts are estranged and resentful; third, he suffers the trouble of being held back; fourth, heaven has taken his wits.

sentences.zh: 本慮其剽勇輕速，掩襲未備，決於一戰；

translations.literal: We had feared his fierce courage and swift strike, that he would raid us unprepared and settle all in one battle;
translations.idiomatic: We had feared his fierce courage and swift strike, that he would raid us unprepared and settle all in one battle;

sentences.zh: 今六師齊奮，諸侯同舉，此籠中之鳥耳！」

translations.literal: now the six armies rise together and the lords act as one—this is a bird in a cage!
translations.idiomatic: now the six armies rise together and the lords act as one—this is a bird in a cage!"

sentences.zh: 蕭賾問攸之於周山圖，山圖曰：「攸之相與鄰鄉，數共征伐，頗悉其為人，性度險刻，士心不附，今頓兵堅城之下，適所以為離散之漸耳。」

translations.literal: Xiao Ze asked Zhou Shantu about Youzhi; Shantu said: "Youzhi and I are neighbors by origin; we have campaigned together many times, and I know his ways well. His nature is treacherous and harsh, and soldiers' hearts do not cling to him. Now he halts his army beneath a strong wall—this is precisely the beginning of dissolution."
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Ze asked Zhou Shantu about Youzhi. Shantu said: "Youzhi and I are neighbors by origin; we have campaigned together many times, and I know his ways well. His nature is treacherous and harsh, and soldiers' hearts do not cling to him. Now he halts his army beneath a strong wall—this is precisely the beginning of dissolution."

sentences.zh: 蒼梧王下升明二年（

translations.literal: Deposed Emperor of Cangwu, lower scroll, second year of Shengming (
translations.idiomatic: Deposed Emperor of Cangwu, lower scroll, second year of Shengming (

sentences.zh: 戊午，公元四七八年）

translations.literal: wuwu, 478 CE)
translations.idiomatic: wuwu, 478 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，巳酉朔，百官戎服入朝。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on yiyou the new moon, the hundred officials entered court in military dress.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on yiyou the new moon, the hundred officials entered court in military dress.

sentences.zh: 沈攸之盡銳攻郢城，柳世隆乘間屢破之。

translations.literal: Shen Youzhi mustered his elite to assault Ying city; Liu Shilong seized openings and repeatedly defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Youzhi mustered his elite to assault Ying city; Liu Shilong seized openings and repeatedly defeated him.

sentences.zh: 蕭賾遣軍主桓敬等入軍據西塞，為世隆聲援。

translations.literal: Xiao Ze sent the army commander Huan Jing and others to enter the army and hold Xisai, lending Shilong support.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Ze sent army commander Huan Jing and others to enter the army and hold Xisai, lending Shilong support.

sentences.zh: 攸之獲郢府法曹南鄉范雲，使送書入城，餉武陵王贊犢一腔，柳世隆魚三十尾，皆去其首。

translations.literal: Youzhi captured Fan Yun of Nanxiang, law clerk of the Ying headquarters, and had him carry a letter into the city, sending Prince Wuling Zan a calf and Liu Shilong thirty fish—all beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi captured Fan Yun of Nanxiang, law clerk of the Ying headquarters, and had him carry a letter into the city, sending Prince Wuling Zan a calf and Liu Shilong thirty fish—all beheaded.

sentences.zh: 城中欲殺之，雲曰：「老母弱弟，懸命沈氏，若違其命，禍必及親；

translations.literal: Those in the city wished to kill him; Yun said: "My aged mother and weak younger brother hang their lives on the Shen clan; if I disobey their order, disaster will reach my kin;
translations.idiomatic: Those in the city wished to kill him. Yun said: "My aged mother and weak younger brother hang their lives on the Shen clan; if I disobey their order, disaster will reach my kin;

sentences.zh: 今日就戮，甘心如薺。」

translations.literal: to die today—I would accept the blade as gladly as shepherd's purse."
translations.idiomatic: to die today—I would accept the blade as gladly as shepherd's purse."

sentences.zh: 乃赦之。

translations.literal: They thereupon pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: They thereupon pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 攸之遣其將皇甫仲賢向武昌，中兵參軍公孫方平向西陽。

translations.literal: Youzhi sent his general Huangfu Zhongxian toward Wuchang and the middle army adjutant Gongsun Fangping toward Xiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi sent his general Huangfu Zhongxian toward Wuchang and middle army adjutant Gongsun Fangping toward Xiyang.

sentences.zh: 武昌太守臧渙降於攸之，西陽太守王毓奔湓城。

translations.literal: Wuchang's governor Zang Huan surrendered to Youzhi; Xiyang's governor Wang Yu fled to Pencheng.
translations.idiomatic: Wuchang governor Zang Huan surrendered to Youzhi; Xiyang governor Wang Yu fled to Pencheng.

sentences.zh: 方平據西陽，豫州刺史劉懷珍遣建寧太守張謨等，將萬人擊之。

translations.literal: Fangping held Xiyang; the governor of Yu, Liu Huaizhen, sent the governor of Jianning Zhang Mo and others with ten thousand men to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Fangping held Xiyang. Yu governor Liu Huaizhen sent Jianning governor Zhang Mo and others with ten thousand men to attack him.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，方平敗走。

translations.literal: On xinyou Fangping was defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou Fangping was defeated and fled.

sentences.zh: 平西將軍黃回等軍至西陽，溯流而進。

translations.literal: The general who calms the west Huang Hui and others reached Xiyang and advanced upstream.
translations.idiomatic: General who calms the west Huang Hui and others reached Xiyang and advanced upstream.

sentences.zh: 攸之素失人情，但劫以威力。

translations.literal: Youzhi had long lost men's hearts and ruled only by coerced might.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi had long lost men's hearts and ruled only by coerced might.

sentences.zh: 初發江陵，日有逃者；

translations.literal: When he first set out from Jiangling, there were deserters every day;
translations.idiomatic: When he first set out from Jiangling, there were deserters every day;

sentences.zh: 及攻郢城，三十餘日不拔，逃者稍多；

translations.literal: when the assault on Ying city went more than thirty days without success, deserters grew more numerous;
translations.idiomatic: when the assault on Ying city went more than thirty days without success, deserters grew more numerous;

sentences.zh: 攸之日夕乘馬歷營撫慰，而去者不息。

translations.literal: Youzhi rode his horse through the camps morning and evening to comfort them, yet those who left did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi rode his horse through the camps morning and evening to comfort them, yet those who left did not cease.

sentences.zh: 攸之大怒，召諸軍主曰：「我被太后令，建義下都。

translations.literal: Youzhi grew greatly angry and summoned the army commanders, saying: "I received the empress dowager's order to raise righteousness and march on the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi grew greatly angry and summoned the army commanders, saying: "I received the empress dowager's order to raise righteousness and march on the capital.

sentences.zh: 大事若克，白紗帽共著耳；

translations.literal: If the great affair succeeds, we shall all wear the white gauze cap together;
translations.idiomatic: If the great affair succeeds, we shall all wear the white gauze cap together;

sentences.zh: 如其不振，朝廷自誅我百口，不關餘人。

translations.literal: if it fails to rise, the court will execute my hundred mouths itself—it concerns no one else.
translations.idiomatic: if it fails to rise, the court will execute my hundred mouths itself—it concerns no one else.

sentences.zh: 比軍人叛散，皆卿等不以為意。

translations.literal: Yet soldiers desert—you commanders treat it as nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Yet soldiers desert—you commanders treat it as nothing.

sentences.zh: 我亦不能問叛身，自今軍中有叛者，軍主任其罪。」

translations.literal: I cannot pursue every deserter myself; from now on, if anyone deserts within an army, that army's commander bears the guilt."
translations.idiomatic: I cannot pursue every deserter myself; from now on, if anyone deserts within an army, that army's commander bears the guilt."

sentences.zh: 於是一人叛，遣人追之，亦去不返，莫敢發覺，鹹有異計。

translations.literal: Thereupon one man deserted; they sent men to pursue him, but he too left and did not return. No one dared report it—all began to harbor other designs.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon one man deserted; they sent men after him, but he too left and never came back. No one dared report it, and all began to plot other courses.

sentences.zh: 劉攘兵射書入城請降，柳世隆開門納之；

translations.literal: Liu Rangbing shot a letter into the city asking to surrender; Liu Shilong opened the gates and admitted him;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Rangbing shot a letter into the city offering surrender; Liu Shilong opened the gates and let him in;

sentences.zh: 丁卯夜，攘兵燒營而去。

translations.literal: On the night of dingmao, Rangbing burned the camp and departed.
translations.idiomatic: That night, on dingmao, Rangbing burned the camp and left.

sentences.zh: 軍中見火起，爭棄甲走，將帥不能禁。

translations.literal: When the army saw fire break out, they scrambled to cast off armor and flee; commanders could not restrain them.
translations.idiomatic: When the troops saw the fire, they cast off their armor and fled in a rush; the commanders could not stop them.

sentences.zh: 攸之聞之，怒，銜須咀之，收攘兵兄子天賜、女婿張平虜，斬之。

translations.literal: When Youzhi heard of it, he grew angry, gnawed his beard in rage, seized Rangbing's nephew Tiansi and son-in-law Zhang Pinglu, and beheaded them.
translations.idiomatic: When Youzhi heard of it, he flew into a rage, gnawed his beard, seized Rangbing's nephew Tiansi and son-in-law Zhang Pinglu, and had them beheaded.

sentences.zh: 向旦，攸之帥眾過江，至魯山，軍遂大散，諸將皆走。

translations.literal: Toward dawn, Youzhi led his forces across the river to Lushan; the army then broke up in mass dispersal, and all the generals fled.
translations.idiomatic: Toward dawn Youzhi led his men across the river to Lushan; the army then scattered completely, and all the generals fled.

sentences.zh: 臧寅曰：「幸其成而棄其敗，吾不忍為也！」

translations.literal: Zang Yin said: "To rejoice in success yet abandon it in defeat—such I cannot bear to do!"
translations.idiomatic: Zang Yin said: "To share in victory yet flee from defeat—such I cannot bear to do!"

sentences.zh: 乃投水死。

translations.literal: Thereupon he threw himself into the water and died.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he threw himself into the water and died.

sentences.zh: 攸之猶有數十騎自隨，宣令軍中曰：「荊州城中大有錢，可相與還，取以為資糧。」

translations.literal: Youzhi still had several dozen horsemen following him. He proclaimed throughout the army: "There is much money in Jing province's capital city—we can return together and take it for supplies."
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi still had several dozen horsemen with him. He announced to the army: "There is a great deal of money in the Jing province capital—we can go back together and take it for supplies."

sentences.zh: 郢城未有追軍，而散軍畏蠻抄，更相聚結，可二萬人，隨攸之還江陵。

translations.literal: Ying city had no pursuing forces yet; the scattered troops, fearing savage raids, regrouped again—about twenty thousand—and followed Youzhi back to Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: Ying city had no pursuing force yet, but the scattered soldiers, fearing raids by the barbarians, gathered again—about twenty thousand in all—and followed Youzhi back to Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 張敬兒既斬攸之使者，即勒兵；

translations.literal: After Zhang Jinger had beheaded Youzhi's messenger, he immediately mobilized his troops;
translations.idiomatic: After Zhang Jinger had killed Youzhi's messenger, he immediately mobilized his troops;

sentences.zh: 偵攸之下，遂襲江陵。

translations.literal: learning that Youzhi had descended, he then struck Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: and when he learned that Youzhi had moved downstream, he struck Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 攸之使子元琰與兼長史江乂、別駕傅宣共守江陵城。

translations.literal: Youzhi had sent his son Yuanyan together with the acting chief administrator Jiang Yi and the registrar Fu Xuan to hold Jiangling city jointly.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi had left his son Yuanyan, together with acting chief administrator Jiang Yi and registrar Fu Xuan, to hold Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 敬兒至沙橋，觀望未進。

translations.literal: Jinger reached Shaqiao and watched without advancing.
translations.idiomatic: Jinger reached Shaqiao and waited without advancing.

sentences.zh: 城中夜聞鶴唳，謂為軍來，乂、宣開門出走，吏民崩潰。

translations.literal: In the city at night they heard cranes calling and took it for the army's arrival; Yi and Xuan opened the gates and fled, and officials and commoners collapsed in disorder.
translations.idiomatic: At night the city heard cranes calling and took it for an approaching army; Yi and Xuan opened the gates and fled, and officials and commoners broke in panic.

sentences.zh: 元琰奔寵洲，為人所殺。

translations.literal: Yuanyan fled toward Chongzhou and was killed by someone.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanyan fled toward Chongzhou and was killed.

sentences.zh: 敬兒至江陵，誅攸之二子、四孫。

translations.literal: Jinger reached Jiangling and executed Youzhi's two sons and four grandsons.
translations.idiomatic: When Jinger reached Jiangling, he executed Youzhi's two sons and four grandsons.

sentences.zh: 攸之將至江陵百餘里，聞城已為敬兒所據，士卒隨之者皆散。

translations.literal: When Youzhi was still a hundred-plus li from Jiangling, he learned the city had already been seized by Jinger, and all the soldiers following him dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: When Youzhi was still more than a hundred li from Jiangling, he learned the city had already fallen to Jinger, and all the soldiers who had followed him scattered.

sentences.zh: 攸之無所歸，與其子文和走至華容界，皆縊於櫟林；

translations.literal: With nowhere to go, Youzhi fled with his son Wenhe to the border of Huarong and both hanged themselves in an oak grove;
translations.idiomatic: With nowhere left to go, Youzhi fled with his son Wenhe to the border of Huarong, and both hanged themselves in an oak grove;

sentences.zh: 己巳，村民斬首送江陵。

translations.literal: On jisi, villagers severed their heads and sent them to Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi villagers cut off their heads and sent them to Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 敬兒擎之以楯，覆以青絲，徇諸市郭，乃送建康。

translations.literal: Jinger held them up on a shield, covered them with green silk, paraded them through the markets, and then sent them to Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: Jinger held the heads up on a shield, covered them with green silk, paraded them through the towns, and then sent them to Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 敬兒誅攸之親黨，收其財物數十萬，皆以入私。

translations.literal: Jinger executed Youzhi's kin and associates, seized their property worth several hundred thousand, and kept it all for himself.
translations.idiomatic: Jinger executed Youzhi's kin and followers, seized property worth several hundred thousand, and kept it all for himself.

sentences.zh: 初，倉曹參軍金城邊榮，為府錄事所辱，攸之為榮鞭殺錄事。

translations.literal: Earlier, Bian Rong of Jincheng, a staff officer in the granary bureau, had been humiliated by the registrar of the governor's office; Youzhi had the registrar flogged to death on Bian Rong's behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Bian Rong of Jincheng, a granary bureau staff officer, had been humiliated by the governor's registrar; Youzhi had the registrar flogged to death on Rong's behalf.

sentences.zh: 及敬兒將至，榮為留府司馬，或說之使詣敬兒降，榮曰：「受沈公厚恩，共如此大事，一朝緩急，便易本心，吾不能也！」

translations.literal: When Jinger was about to arrive, Rong was serving as deputy of the garrison left at the office. Some urged him to go surrender to Jinger. Rong said: "I received great kindness from Lord Shen and joined in this great undertaking; at the first turn of fortune to change my heart—I cannot!"
translations.idiomatic: When Jinger was about to arrive, Rong was serving as deputy of the garrison left behind. Some urged him to go surrender to Jinger.
